lesson_plan:
School Name
Teacher Name
Subject English
Grade Level Grade 7
Date
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Lesson Plan Type D-DLP
Difficulty Basic
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Types of characters in literature
Performance Standards Character analysis and identification
Learning Competencies MELC Code: ENG7LC-Ia-1: Analyzes the character's traits, motivations, and relationships in a literary text
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to understand the different types of characters in literature, such as protagonist, antagonist, and supporting characters.
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to demonstrate their understanding of character types by creating a simple character map.
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the importance of character analysis in understanding literary texts.
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Types of Characters
References DepEd English Grade 7 Learner's Material. DepEd.
Materials Whiteboard, markers, character map templates, literature samples
Values Infused Critical thinking, analysis, and appreciation of literary texts
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
DepEd English Grade 7 Learner's Material A comprehensive guide to English language and literature for Grade 7 students
Character Map Templates Pre-designed templates for creating character maps
Literature Samples Selected literary texts for analysis and discussion
Whiteboard and Markers For note-taking and illustration purposes
Online Resources Supplementary online materials for further learning and research
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray together, led by our class president." Greetings: "Good morning, class." Classroom Management: "Please take out your materials and get ready for the lesson." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and report attendance.
Review "What are the elements of a short story?" "Can you give an example of a character in a story?" "How do authors use characters to convey themes?" Students recall the elements of a short story, provide examples of characters, and explain how authors use characters to convey themes.
Motivation "Character Charades": Divide the class into two teams and have them act out different types of characters (e.g. protagonist, antagonist, supporting character) without speaking. The team that guesses the most characters correctly wins. Students participate in the game, demonstrating their understanding of character types and having fun while learning.
Lesson Proper Define the key concept of character types, provide examples, and ask questions to clarify understanding. "What is a protagonist?" "Can you give an example of a protagonist in a story?" Students understand the definition of protagonist, provide examples, and demonstrate their understanding of character types.
Application Divide the class into groups and assign each group a different literary text. Ask them to create a character map, identifying the protagonist, antagonist, and supporting characters. Provide a rubric with criteria such as accuracy, completeness, and creativity. Students create a character map, demonstrating their understanding of character types and their ability to analyze literary texts.
Generalization "What did you learn about character types today?" "How can you apply this knowledge in your own writing or analysis of literary texts?" "Why is it important to understand character types in literature?" Students reflect on their learning, demonstrate their understanding of character types, and explain the importance of analyzing characters in literary texts.
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items Description
1. What are the two main types of characters in a story? Protagonist and Antagonist
2. What is the role of a static character in a story? Remains the same throughout the story
3. What is the role of a dynamic character in a story? Changes or grows throughout the story
4. What is the difference between a major and minor character? Major characters play a significant role, while minor characters play a lesser role
5. How do characters contribute to the plot of a story? Characters' actions and decisions drive the plot forward
ANSWER KEY
1. Protagonist and Antagonist 5. Characters' actions and decisions drive the plot forward
2. Remains the same throughout the story 4. Major characters play a significant role, while minor characters play a lesser role
3. Changes or grows throughout the story
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Description
Create a character map Identify the protagonist, antagonist, and supporting characters in a given story. Analyze their roles and relationships.
Rubric: Content (40%), Organization (30%), and Presentation (30%)
Submission: Due next meeting, in printed or digital format
VII. REMARKS
Observations Description
Delivery The lesson was delivered at a moderate pace, with opportunities for student participation and engagement.
Pacing The lesson was well-paced, with adequate time allocated for each activity and discussion.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection Description
What worked well: The students were engaged and participative during the discussion on character types.
What to improve: More time could be allocated for the students to work on the character map activity.
Next session focus: To delve deeper into the analysis of character relationships and their impact on the plot.

lesson_plan:
School Name
Teacher Name
Subject Science
Grade Level Grade 1
Date
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Lesson Plan Type D-DLP
Difficulty Basic
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Characteristics and needs of plants
Performance Standards Identifying and describing the basic parts of plants
Learning Competencies SC1PS-1a: Recognize the basic needs of plants
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to recall the basic parts of plants
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to demonstrate how to plant a seed
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the importance of plants in our environment
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Plants
References K to 12 Science Curriculum Guide. Department of Education.
Materials Pictures of different plants, plant seeds, soil, pots
Values Infused Responsibility, care for the environment
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
Textbook Grade 1 Science textbook
Pictures of plants Printed pictures of different types of plants
Plant seeds Seeds for planting activity
Soil and pots Materials for planting activity
Whiteboard and markers For discussion and illustration
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray, who can lead us in prayer?" Greetings: "Good morning class, how are you today?" Classroom Management: "Please take out your materials and get ready for the lesson." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and report attendance
Review "What do plants need to grow? What are the parts of a plant?" Students recall that plants need water, sunlight, and air to grow, and identify the basic parts of a plant such as roots, stem, and leaves
Motivation Activity title: "Plant Exploration". Show pictures of different plants and ask students to share what they know about plants. Explain the importance of plants in our environment. Students share their prior knowledge about plants and understand the significance of plants
Lesson Proper Define the key concept of plants, show examples of different plants, and explain their basic needs. Ask questions like "What do you think plants need to grow?" and "Can you name a type of plant?" Students understand the definition and basic needs of plants, identify different types of plants, and participate in the discussion
Application Activity title: "Planting a Seed". Divide the class into groups and provide each group with a pot, soil, and a seed. Instruct them to plant the seed and explain the process. Rubric: participation (20 points), correct planting process (30 points), and group cooperation (50 points) Students plant a seed correctly and demonstrate understanding of the planting process
Generalization "What did you learn about plants today? How can you apply what you learned in taking care of plants? Why are plants important to us?" Students recall what they learned about plants, explain how they can apply their knowledge, and understand the importance of plants
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation ItemsDescription
1. What are the basic needs of plants?Students should be able to identify water, sunlight, air, and soil as the basic needs of plants.
2. What is the function of roots in plants?Students should be able to explain that roots help plants absorb water and nutrients from the soil.
3. What is photosynthesis and why is it important for plants?Students should be able to explain that photosynthesis is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and air, and that it is important for plant growth and survival.
4. What are the different parts of a plant and their functions?Students should be able to identify and describe the functions of the roots, stem, leaves, and flowers of a plant.
5. Why are plants important to humans and the environment?Students should be able to explain that plants provide oxygen, food, shelter, and habitat for various organisms, and help regulate the climate and water cycle.
ANSWER KEY
1. Water, sunlight, air, and soil
2. To absorb water and nutrients from the soil
3. The process by which plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and air
4. Roots (absorb water and nutrients), stem (supports the plant), leaves (make food through photosynthesis), flowers (produce seeds)
5. Plants provide oxygen, food, shelter, and habitat for various organisms, and help regulate the climate and water cycle
VI. ASSIGNMENT
TaskDescription
Draw and label the different parts of a plantStudents should draw a diagram of a plant and label its roots, stem, leaves, and flowers. The diagram should be colored and include a short paragraph explaining the function of each part.
Rubric:Accuracy of labeling (30%), completeness of diagram (20%), creativity and neatness (30%), written explanation (20%)
Due date:Next meeting
VII. REMARKS
ObservationsDescription
DeliveryThe lesson was delivered at a moderate pace, allowing students to absorb the information. However, some students seemed to lose focus during the discussion of photosynthesis.
PacingThe lesson was completed within the allotted 45 minutes, but some activities could have been allocated more time to allow for better understanding and participation.
VIII. REFLECTION
ReflectionDescription
What worked well:The use of visual aids and hands-on activities helped to engage the students and facilitate their understanding of the topic.

Resource Description
Science textbook Grade 1 Science textbook by DepEd
Pictures of plants Printed pictures of different types of plants
Seeds and soil Seeds and soil for planting activity
Gardening tools Small gardening tools for students to use

IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray, led by Juan." Greetings: "Good morning, class." Classroom Management: "Please sit properly and get out your materials." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, sit properly, and get out their materials. Class secretary reports the attendance.
Review "What are the basic needs of plants?" "What do plants need to grow?" Students recall the basic needs of plants, such as water, sunlight, and air.
Motivation Activity title: "Planting a Seed" - Students plant a seed in a pot and observe its growth. Mechanics: Give each student a pot, soil, and a seed. Have them plant the seed and water it. Students participate in the planting activity and observe the growth of the seed.
Lesson Proper Define the key concept of plants: "Plants are living things that grow in the ground." Give examples: "Trees, flowers, and grass are all plants." Ask questions: "What are the parts of a plant?" "What do plants need to grow?" Students recall the definition of plants, identify the parts of a plant, and describe what plants need to grow.
Application Activity title: "Plant Parts" - Divide the class into groups and give each group a picture of a plant. Ask them to identify and label the different parts of the plant. Rubric: Accuracy of labeling (3 points), completeness of labeling (2 points), teamwork (2 points), and presentation (3 points). Students identify and label the different parts of the plant, such as roots, stem, and leaves.
Generalization "What did you learn about plants today?" "How can you take care of plants at home?" "Why are plants important to us?" Students recall what they learned about plants, describe how to take care of plants, and explain the importance of plants.

Evaluation Items Description
1. What are the basic needs of plants? Students should be able to identify the basic needs of plants such as water, sunlight, air, and soil.

3. What is photosynthesis and why is it important for plants? Students should be able to explain that photosynthesis is the process by which plants make their own food from sunlight, water, and air, and that it is essential for plant growth and survival.
4. What are the different parts of a plant and their functions? Students should be able to identify and describe the functions of the roots, stem, leaves, and flowers of a plant.
5. Why are plants important to our environment? Students should be able to explain that plants are important because they provide oxygen, food, and shelter for many living organisms, and help to maintain a healthy environment.
ANSWER KEY
1. Water, sunlight, air, and soil
2. To absorb water and nutrients from the soil
3. The process by which plants make their own food from sunlight, water, and air
4. Roots - absorb water and nutrients, Stem - supports the plant, Leaves - make food through photosynthesis, Flowers - produce seeds
5. They provide oxygen, food, and shelter for many living organisms, and help to maintain a healthy environment
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Description
Draw and label the different parts of a plant Students should draw a diagram of a plant and label its different parts, including the roots, stem, leaves, and flowers. The diagram should be colored and include a short paragraph describing the function of each part.
Rubric: Accuracy of labeling (30 points), completeness of diagram (20 points), creativity and neatness (30 points), paragraph description (20 points)
Due date: Next meeting

Observations Description
Delivery The lesson was delivered at a pace that was suitable for the students, and the teacher was able to engage the students throughout the lesson.
Pacing The lesson was well-paced, with adequate time allocated for each activity and discussion. However, some students needed more time to complete the drawing task.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection Description
What worked well The students were engaged and interested in the topic of plants, and the hands-on activity of drawing and labeling the different parts of a plant was effective in reinforcing their understanding.
What to improve More time could be allocated for the drawing task, and additional visual aids could be used to support the lesson and make it more interactive.
Next session focus The next session will focus on the importance of plants in our environment, and the students will participate in a group discussion on how they can help to protect and conserve plants in their community.

lesson_plan:
English
Grade 7
1 45 Minutes
Types of Characters
Intermediate
K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
D-DLP
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Students will be able to identify and describe the different types of characters in a story.
Performance Standards Students will be able to analyze and evaluate the characteristics of different types of characters.
Learning Competencies MA.7.1: Analyze and interpret literary texts using appropriate literary devices and techniques.
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to identify and describe the characteristics of different types of characters, such as protagonists, antagonists, and supporting characters.
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to create a character chart to illustrate the characteristics of different types of characters.
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the importance of understanding different types of characters in a story.
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Types of Characters
References DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020: K-12 Curriculum Guide for English
Materials Whiteboard, markers, handouts with character charts, examples of stories with different types of characters
Values Infused Empathy and understanding of different perspectives
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
Textbook English Language Arts for Grade 7
Handouts Character charts and examples of stories with different types of characters
Whiteboard For illustrating and explaining different types of characters
Markers For writing and illustrating on the whiteboard
Examples of Stories With different types of characters, such as Romeo and Juliet, The Hunger Games, and To Kill a Mockingbird
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Who would like to lead the prayer today?" "I would like to lead the prayer today."
Greetings: "Good morning, class. How are you all doing today?" "I'm good, thank you."
Classroom Management: "Please take out your handouts and get ready to take notes." "I have my handout. I'm ready."
Attendance: "Ms. Secretary, can you please report the attendance?" "Yes, I have the attendance report."
Review Question 1: "What is a character in a story?" "A character is a person or animal in a story."
Question 2: "What is the difference between a protagonist and an antagonist?" "A protagonist is the main character, and an antagonist is the bad guy."
Motivation Activity: "Character Charades" - Students act out different types of characters, and their classmates have to guess who they are. "I'm the protagonist! I'm the main character."
Lesson Proper Definition: "A character is a person or animal in a story who has their own thoughts, feelings, and actions." "I understand. A character is someone who has their own thoughts and feelings."
Examples: "Romeo is a protagonist, and Tybalt is an antagonist in Romeo and Juliet." "I see. Romeo is the good guy, and Tybalt is the bad guy."
Application Activity: "Character Chart" - Students create a chart to illustrate the characteristics of different types of characters. "I have a chart with the characteristics of protagonists, antagonists, and supporting characters."
Rubric: "Character Chart Rubric" - Students will be evaluated based on the completeness and accuracy of their charts. "I understand the rubric. I'll make sure to complete my chart accurately."
Generalization Question 1: "What did you learn about characters today?" "I learned that characters are people or animals in a story who have their own thoughts, feelings, and actions."
Question 2: "How can you apply what you learned about characters to real life?" "I can apply what I learned by being more empathetic towards others and understanding their perspectives."
Question 3: "Why is it important to understand characters in a story?" "It's important to understand characters because it helps me connect with the story and understand the author's message."
V. EVALUATION
Item Description
1 What is a character in a story?
2 What is the difference between a protagonist and an antagonist?
3 What are the characteristics of a protagonist?
4 What are the characteristics of an antagonist?
5 What are the characteristics of a supporting character?
ANSWER KEY
1 A character is a person or animal in a story who has their own thoughts, feelings, and actions.
2 A protagonist is the main character, and an antagonist is the bad guy.
3 A protagonist is a character who is the main hero of the story.
4 An antagonist is a character who is the main obstacle or villain of the story.
5 A supporting character is a character who helps or supports the protagonist in the story.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Description
Create a character chart to illustrate the characteristics of different types of characters. Deadline: Next class meeting. Rubric: "Character Chart Rubric" - Students will be evaluated based on the completeness and accuracy of their charts.
VII. REMARKS
Observation Description
Students were engaged and participated actively in the lesson. The students showed a good understanding of the different types of characters and their characteristics.
The teacher provided clear explanations and examples to support the students' understanding. The students were able to apply what they learned to real-life situations.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection Description
I was pleased to see the students actively participating in the lesson and showing a good understanding of the different types of characters. I will continue to provide clear explanations and examples to support the students' understanding and application of what they learn.
I will also make sure to provide opportunities for students to apply what they learn to real-life situations. I will continue to assess the students' understanding and adjust my teaching strategies as needed.

Subject Matter Types of Characters

Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response

Attendance: "Ms. Secretary, can you please report the attendance?" "Yes, I have the attendance report."

Question 2: "What is the difference between a protagonist and an antagonist?" "A protagonist is the main character, and an antagonist is the bad guy."
Motivation Activity: "Character Charades" - Students act out different types of characters, and their classmates have to guess who they are. "I'm the protagonist! I'm the main character."

Application Activity: "Character Chart" - Students create a chart to illustrate the characteristics of different types of characters. "I have a chart with the characteristics of protagonists, antagonists, and supporting characters."

School Name
Teacher Name
Subject Mathematics
Grade Level Grade 4
Date
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Lesson Plan Type D-DLP
Difficulty Intermediate
Curriculum MATATAG Curriculum (DepEd Order No. 10, s. 2024)
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Types of animals and their characteristics
Performance Standards Classification of animals based on their habitats
Learning Competencies MELC Code: M4NS-IIIa-1: Describes the basic needs of animals
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to identify and explain the different types of animal habitats
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to demonstrate how to classify animals into their respective habitats
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the importance of preserving animal habitats
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Animals
References DepEd Order No. 10, s. 2024: MATATAG Curriculum
Materials Pictures of different animals, animal habitat diagrams, whiteboard and markers
Values Infused Respect for animal life and preservation of their habitats
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
National Geographic Kids Online resource for animal pictures and information
Animal Habitat Diagrams Printable diagrams of different animal habitats
Whiteboard and Markers For note-taking and illustration of animal habitats
Animal Picture Cards For classification activity
DepEd Learning Portal Online resource for lesson plans and educational materials
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray, led by Juan." Greetings: "Good morning, class." Classroom Management: "Please take out your notebooks and pencils." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and report attendance
Review "What are the basic needs of animals?" "What do animals need to survive?" "Can you give examples of animal habitats?" Students recall the basic needs of animals, such as food, water, shelter, and air, and give examples of different animal habitats
Motivation Activity title: "Animal Habitat Sorting Game". Instructions: "Sort the animal pictures into their respective habitats." Connection to topic: "This game will help us understand the different types of animal habitats and how animals adapt to their environments." Students participate in the sorting game and begin to understand the concept of animal habitats
Lesson Proper Definition of animal habitats, examples of different habitats, teacher questions: "What are some characteristics of a desert habitat?" "How do animals adapt to their habitats?" Students learn about the different types of animal habitats, such as desert, forest, and ocean, and understand how animals adapt to their environments
Application Activity title: "Animal Habitat Diorama". Instructions: "Create a diorama of an animal habitat using a shoe box and materials." Division of class: "Work in groups of 3-4." Group tasks: "Each group will create a diorama of a different animal habitat." Rubric: "Creativity (30 points), Accuracy (30 points), Teamwork (20 points), Presentation (20 points)" Students create a diorama of an animal habitat and demonstrate their understanding of the concept
Generalization "What did you learn about animal habitats today?" "How can you apply what you learned to real-life situations?" "Why is it important to preserve animal habitats?" Students reflect on what they learned, think about how to apply their knowledge, and understand the importance of preserving animal habitats
Subject: Mathematics
Grade Level: Grade 4
Topic: Animals
Quarter: 1
Duration: 45 Minutes
Difficulty: Intermediate
Curriculum: MATATAG Curriculum (DepEd Order No. 10, s. 2024)
Lesson Plan Type: D-DLP
V. EVALUATION
No. Item
1. What is the main characteristic of a mammal?
2. What is the difference between a carnivore and a herbivore?
3. What is the purpose of a bird's beak?
4. What is the main source of food for a fish?
5. What is the unique feature of a reptile's skin?
ANSWER KEY
1. Mammals have hair and produce milk for their young.
2. Carnivores eat meat, while herbivores eat plants.
3. A bird's beak is used for eating and preening.
4. Fish eat plankton, algae, and small animals.
5. Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Rubric
Draw a picture of your favorite animal and label its different parts. Creativity (30 points), Accuracy (30 points), Completeness (40 points)
VII. REMARKS
Observation Action
The teacher delivered the lesson at a good pace. Continue to monitor the class's understanding.
Some students seemed confused during the discussion. Provide additional support and review the material.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection Action
The lesson on animals was engaging and informative. Continue to incorporate hands-on activities and real-world examples.
Some students struggled with the vocabulary. Provide additional support and review the material.
The class discussion was productive and helped clarify any misconceptions. Continue to encourage class discussion and participation.

Subject Science

Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Lesson Plan Type D-DLP
Difficulty Basic
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Characteristics of planets in our solar system
Performance Standards Identifying the planets in our solar system
Learning Competencies SC2PS-2a: Demonstrates an understanding of the basic concepts of astronomy
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to recall the names of the planets in our solar system
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to demonstrate the relative positions of the planets in our solar system
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the uniqueness of each planet in our solar system
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Planets
References DepEd Science Grade 2 Learner's Material. Department of Education. 2020.
Materials Pictures of the planets, solar system model, whiteboard and markers
Values Infused Curiosity, appreciation for the wonders of the universe
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
DepEd Science Grade 2 Learner's Material A comprehensive learning material for Grade 2 students covering the topic of planets
Solar System Model A 3D model of the solar system to help students visualize the relative positions of the planets
Pictures of the Planets Actual pictures of the planets to help students identify and describe their characteristics
Whiteboard and Markers For the teacher to write notes and draw diagrams during the lesson
Internet Connection For the teacher to access online resources and videos about the planets
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray together, led by Juan." Greetings: "Good morning, class." Classroom Management: "Please take out your science notebooks and pencils." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and report the attendance
Review "What is the solar system?" "What are the planets we have discussed so far?" The solar system is the collection of celestial objects that orbit the sun. We have discussed Mercury and Venus.
Motivation Activity title: "Planet Scavenger Hunt". Instructions: "Find and identify the pictures of the planets around the classroom." Connection to topic: "This activity will help you become familiar with the different planets in our solar system." Students participate in the scavenger hunt and identify the pictures of the planets
Lesson Proper Definition of planets: "A planet is a large celestial body that orbits the sun." Examples: "Earth, Mars, Jupiter". Teacher questions: "What is the largest planet in our solar system?" "What is the smallest planet in our solar system?" A planet is a large celestial body that orbits the sun. Jupiter is the largest planet. Mercury is the smallest planet.
Application Activity title: "Planet Sorting". Instructions: "Sort the pictures of the planets into two groups: rocky planets and gas planets." Division of the class: "Work in pairs to sort the pictures." Rubric: "Accuracy of sorting (2 points), teamwork (1 point)" Students sort the pictures of the planets into rocky planets (Mercury, Mars, Earth) and gas planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune)
Generalization Cognitive question: "What did you learn about the planets today?" Psychomotor question: "Can you show me the relative positions of the planets in our solar system?" Affective question: "Why do you think it's important to learn about the planets?" I learned that there are eight planets in our solar system. I can show you the relative positions of the planets. It's important to learn about the planets because they are part of our universe and affect our daily lives.
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items Description

lesson_plan:
School Name
Teacher Name
Subject Science
Grade Level Grade 10
Date
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Lesson Plan Type D-DLP
Difficulty Basic
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Characteristics and functions of plants
Performance Standards Identification and classification of plant types
Learning Competencies SC10-PS-12: Explains the importance of plants in the ecosystem
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to analyze the role of plants in the ecosystem
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to demonstrate the process of plant growth
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the importance of plants in their daily lives
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Plants
References DepEd K-12 Science Curriculum Guide. DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020
Materials Pictures of different plant types, plant specimens, whiteboard and markers
Values Infused Appreciation for the importance of plants in the ecosystem
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
Science textbooks Grade 10 Science textbooks with chapters on plants
Online resources National Geographic website with articles on plant types and functions
Plant specimens Real plant specimens for observation and identification
Whiteboard and markers For note-taking and illustration of plant structures
Pictures of plant types For identification and classification of plant types
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray for a productive lesson, led by our class president." Greetings: "Good morning, class." Classroom Management: "Please take out your Science textbooks and get ready for the lesson." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and report attendance
Review "What are the main functions of plants in the ecosystem?" "Can you give examples of plant types and their characteristics?" Students recall the main functions of plants, such as photosynthesis and oxygen production, and give examples of plant types, such as flowering plants and conifers
Motivation Activity title: "Plant Scavenger Hunt". Instructions: "Find and identify different plant types in the school garden." Connection to topic: "This activity will help you recognize and appreciate the diversity of plant life." Students participate in the scavenger hunt, identify plant types, and record their observations
Lesson Proper Definition of plants: "Plants are living organisms that produce their own food through photosynthesis." Examples of plant types: "Flowering plants, conifers, and ferns." Teacher questions: "What are the characteristics of flowering plants?" "How do conifers adapt to their environment?" Students understand the definition of plants, identify characteristics of plant types, and explain adaptations of conifers
Application Activity title: "Plant Classification". Instructions: "Divide into groups and classify plant specimens into their respective types." Rubric: "Accuracy of classification (40 points), teamwork and participation (30 points), and presentation (30 points)" Students classify plant specimens, present their findings, and demonstrate teamwork and participation
Generalization Cognitive question: "What did you learn about the importance of plants in the ecosystem?" Psychomotor question: "How can you apply your knowledge of plant growth and development in your daily life?" Affective question: "Why is it essential to conserve and protect plant species?" Students reflect on their learning, apply their knowledge, and express their appreciation for plant conservation
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items Description
1. What is the main function of roots in plants? To absorb water and nutrients from the soil
2. What is photosynthesis and what is its importance in plants? The process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy, essential for plant growth and energy production
3. What is the role of stomata in plant leaves? To regulate gas exchange, including the release of oxygen and the absorption of carbon dioxide
4. What is the difference between a monocot and a dicot plant? Monocots have one cotyledon, while dicots have two cotyledons, and they also differ in leaf venation and root structure
5. What is the process of transpiration and its significance in plants? The process by which plants release water vapor into the air, essential for maintaining plant temperature and promoting growth
ANSWER KEY
1. To absorb water and nutrients from the soil 5. The process by which plants release water vapor into the air
2. The process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy
3. To regulate gas exchange, including the release of oxygen and the absorption of carbon dioxide
4. Monocots have one cotyledon, while dicots have two cotyledons
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Description
Create a diagram of a plant cell and label its components The diagram should include the cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, and chloroplasts. The student should also provide a brief description of each component's function.
Due Date Next meeting
Rubric Accuracy of diagram (40%), completeness of labels and descriptions (30%), and overall presentation (30%)
VII. REMARKS
Observations Description
Delivery of the lesson The lesson was delivered clearly and concisely, with the teacher providing opportunities for student participation and engagement.
Pacing of the lesson The lesson was well-paced, with the teacher allowing sufficient time for students to complete activities and ask questions.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection Description
What worked well in the lesson The use of visual aids and hands-on activities helped to engage students and promote understanding of plant structures and functions.
What needs improvement More time could be allocated for students to complete the activities and for the teacher to provide individualized feedback.

lesson_plan:
School Name
Teacher Name
Subject Science
Grade Level Grade 2
Date
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Lesson Plan Type D-DLP
Difficulty Basic
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Characteristics of planets in our solar system
Performance Standards Identification of planets and their unique features
Learning Competencies SC2PS-6: Demonstrates an understanding of the basic concepts of astronomy, including the planets and their characteristics
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to recall the names of the planets in our solar system and their relative sizes
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to demonstrate the relative positions of the planets in our solar system using a model or diagram
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the uniqueness of each planet and their importance in our solar system
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Planets
References DepEd Grade 2 Science Learning Materials. Department of Education. https://www.deped.gov.ph/
Materials Pictures and models of the planets, solar system diagram, whiteboard and markers
Values Infused Curiosity, appreciation for the natural world
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
National Geographic Kids Online resource for kid-friendly information about the planets
Solar System Model Kit Hands-on activity for students to build and learn about the planets
Planet Pictures Visual aids for students to identify and learn about the planets
Whiteboard and Markers For note-taking and drawing diagrams of the solar system
Computer or Tablet For accessing online resources and watching educational videos about the planets
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray together, led by Juan." Greetings: "Good morning, class." Classroom Management: "Please take out your science notebooks and pencils." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and report attendance
Review "What is the sun? What are the stars?" The sun is the star at the center of our solar system. Stars are huge balls of hot, glowing gas.
Motivation "Planet Scavenger Hunt": Show pictures of the planets and ask students to identify them. The student who identifies the most planets correctly wins. Students participate in the scavenger hunt, identify the planets, and have fun learning
Lesson Proper Define the key concept of planets: "A planet is a large, rocky or gaseous body that orbits around the sun." Show pictures and models of the planets. Ask questions: "What is the largest planet? What is the smallest planet?" The largest planet is Jupiter. The smallest planet is Mercury. Students learn about the characteristics of the planets.
Application Divide the class into groups and assign each group a planet. Ask them to create a poster or model of their assigned planet, including its unique features. Rubric: Content (40 points), Creativity (30 points), Teamwork (30 points) Students create posters or models of the planets, including their unique features, and present to the class
Generalization "What did you learn about the planets today? How can you apply what you learned in your daily life? Why are the planets important to us?" Students share what they learned, discuss how they can apply it, and explain why the planets are important
V. EVALUATION
Item Description
1. What is the largest planet in our solar system? Jupiter
2. Which planet is known as the Red Planet? Mars
3. What is the planet that we live in? Earth
4. Which planet is the closest to the sun? Mercury
5. What is the farthest planet from the sun? Neptune
ANSWER KEY
1. Jupiter, 2. Mars, 3. Earth, 4. Mercury, 5. Neptune
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Description
Draw and label the planets in our solar system Due next meeting, include the following: planet names, relative sizes, and distances from the sun. Rubric: Accuracy (40%), Neatness (30%), Creativity (30%)
VII. REMARKS
Observation Description
Delivery The lesson was delivered clearly and concisely, with visual aids that helped the students understand the concept of planets.
Pacing The lesson was well-paced, with sufficient time for discussion and activities. However, some students needed more time to complete the tasks.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection Description
The lesson on planets was engaging and informative, with the students showing a keen interest in the topic. What worked well was the use of visual aids and hands-on activities to help the students understand the concept. However, some areas for improvement include providing more time for the students to complete the tasks and incorporating more interactive activities to cater to different learning styles. For the next session, the focus will be on exploring the unique features of each planet and how they differ from one another.

Quarter 1st Quarter

Lesson Plan Type Detailed DLP
Difficulty Intermediate
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Types and functions of nouns in sentences
Performance Standards Identifying and using nouns correctly in context
Learning Competencies 9.1LC1-1: Demonstrates understanding of the concept of nouns and their functions in sentences
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to analyze the types of nouns and their functions in sentences
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to demonstrate the correct usage of nouns in sentences through writing and speaking activities
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the importance of using nouns correctly in communication
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Nouns
References DepEd English Grade 9 Learner's Material. DepEd.
Materials Whiteboard, markers, worksheets, and laptops with internet connection
Values Infused Respect for language and effective communication
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
DepEd English Grade 9 Learner's Material A comprehensive guide to English grammar and usage for Grade 9 students
Online grammar guides Supplementary resources for understanding nouns and their functions
Whiteboard and markers For illustrating examples and notes on nouns
Worksheets For practice exercises on identifying and using nouns correctly
Laptops with internet connection For accessing online resources and activities related to nouns
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray together, led by Juan." Greetings: "Good morning, class." Classroom Management: "Please take out your worksheets and pens." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and report attendance
Review "What are the parts of speech we've discussed so far? Can you give examples of each?" "How do we identify nouns in sentences?" Students recall the parts of speech, provide examples, and explain how to identify nouns
Motivation Activity title: "Noun Scavenger Hunt". Instructions: "Find and write down 5 nouns from the objects in the classroom." Connection to topic: "This activity helps us recognize nouns in our everyday environment." Students participate in the scavenger hunt, identifying and listing nouns
Lesson Proper Definition: "A noun is a word that refers to a person, place, thing, or idea." Examples: "Teacher, Manila, book, love." Questions: "What type of noun is 'city'?" "Can you think of a noun that represents an idea?" Students understand the definition of nouns, provide examples, and answer questions about types of nouns
Application Activity title: "Noun Sorting". Instructions: "Divide into groups and sort these words into types of nouns." Rubric: "Accuracy of sorting (40 points), teamwork (30 points), presentation (30 points)" Students work in groups, sort nouns into categories, and present their work
Generalization Questions: "What did you learn about nouns today?" "How can you apply your understanding of nouns in writing and speaking?" "Why is it important to use nouns correctly in communication?" Students reflect on their learning, think about applications, and consider the importance of correct noun usage
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items Description
1. What is the definition of a noun? A noun is a word that refers to a person, place, thing, or idea.
2. Identify the type of noun: city Proper noun
3. What is a collective noun? A collective noun is a noun that refers to a group of people, animals, or things, such as family, team, or flock.
4. Give an example of an abstract noun Happiness
5. What is the function of a noun in a sentence? A noun can function as a subject, object, or complement in a sentence.
ANSWER KEY
1. A noun is a word that refers to a person, place, thing, or idea.
2. Proper noun
3. A collective noun is a noun that refers to a group of people, animals, or things, such as family, team, or flock.
4. Happiness
5. A noun can function as a subject, object, or complement in a sentence.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Description
Write a short paragraph about a person, place, or thing, using at least 5 different types of nouns (proper, common, collective, abstract, concrete) The paragraph should be at least 5 sentences long and should demonstrate a clear understanding of the different types of nouns. The assignment is due next meeting and will be graded based on the following rubric: content (40%), grammar and mechanics (30%), and creativity (30%).
Rubric:
Content (40%): Does the paragraph demonstrate a clear understanding of the different types of nouns? Are the nouns used correctly and effectively?
Grammar and Mechanics (30%): Is the paragraph free of grammatical errors? Are the sentences well-constructed and easy to understand?
Creativity (30%): Does the paragraph demonstrate creativity and originality in the use of nouns? Are the nouns used in a unique and interesting way?
VII. REMARKS
Observations Description
Delivery The lesson was delivered clearly and concisely, with the teacher providing examples and explanations to help students understand the concept of nouns.
Pacing The lesson was well-paced, with the teacher allowing students to ask questions and participate in discussions without rushing through the material.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection Description
What worked well in the lesson The use of examples and explanations to help students understand the concept of nouns was effective, and the students were able to participate in discussions and ask questions.
What to improve for the next lesson The teacher could provide more opportunities for students to practice using nouns in sentences, and could also provide more feedback to students on their assignments.
Focus for the next session The next session will focus on verbs, and the teacher will provide examples and explanations to help students understand the concept of verbs and how they are used in sentences.

Category Description
Subject Matter Nouns

Values Infused Accuracy, clarity, and respect for language

Resource Description
English Grade 9 Learner's Material A comprehensive guide to English grammar and usage for Grade 9 students
Online Grammar Guides Supplementary online resources for reviewing English grammar rules
Noun Identification Worksheets Practice exercises for identifying and using nouns correctly
Whiteboard and Markers Tools for illustrating and explaining noun concepts on the board
Pencils and Paper Materials for students to complete worksheets and exercises
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer: "Let's pray together, led by Juan." Greetings: "Good morning, class." Classroom Management: "Please take out your English books and worksheets." Attendance: "Please report the attendance, class secretary." Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and report attendance
Review "What are the basic parts of speech?" "Can you give an example of a verb?" "How do adjectives function in a sentence?" Parts of speech include nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc. A verb is an action word, like 'run'. Adjectives describe nouns, like 'happy' in 'happy dog'
Motivation "Noun Scavenger Hunt": Divide the class into small groups and give each a worksheet with different types of nouns (proper, common, collective, abstract). Ask them to find and identify examples of each type of noun in the classroom or school surroundings. Groups identify and list examples of different types of nouns, such as 'Manila' for proper noun, 'dog' for common noun, 'family' for collective noun, and 'happiness' for abstract noun
Lesson Proper Define nouns and their functions, provide examples, and explain the differences between types of nouns. Ask questions like "What is a noun?" and "Can you give an example of a common noun?" A noun is a word that refers to a person, place, thing, or idea. Examples: 'teacher', 'city', 'book', 'love'
Application "Noun Paragraph": Divide the class into groups and ask them to write a short paragraph using at least three different types of nouns. Provide a rubric with criteria such as creativity, grammar, and correct usage of nouns. Groups write paragraphs incorporating various types of nouns, such as 'The beautiful city of Manila is home to many happy families and interesting places like museums and parks'
Generalization "What did you learn about nouns today?" "How can you apply the correct usage of nouns in your daily writing?" "Why is it important to understand the different types of nouns?" Understanding nouns helps in better communication and expression of ideas

3. Essay Explain the difference between a common noun and a proper noun.
4. Identification Identify the nouns in the sentence: 'The happy family visited the beautiful city of Manila.'
5. Fill in the Blanks The _______ noun 'happiness' refers to a feeling or emotion.

lesson_plan:
School Name
Teacher Name
Subject Science
Grade Level Grade 2
Date
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Lesson Plan Type D-DLP
Difficulty Basic
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Names of planets in our solar system
Performance Standards Identifies the planets in our solar system through pictures or models
Learning Competencies SC2PS-2a: Demonstrates an understanding of the basic concepts of astronomy, including the planets in our solar system
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to recall the names of the planets in our solar system
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to point to and identify the planets in a model or picture of the solar system
Affective Objective At the end of the 45-minute lesson, the students must be able to express their wonder and curiosity about the planets in our solar system
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Planets
References DepEd Science Grade 2 Learner's Material. Department of Education. 2020.
Materials Pictures or models of the planets, whiteboard and markers, printed copies of the planets' names
Values Infused Curiosity, wonder, and appreciation for the natural world
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
DepEd Science Grade 2 Learner's Material A textbook that provides an introduction to the planets in our solar system
Pictures or models of the planets Visual aids to help students identify and learn about the planets
Whiteboard and markers Tools for the teacher to write the names of the planets and draw diagrams
Printed copies of the planets' names Handouts for students to refer to during the lesson
Internet connection For the teacher to access online resources and videos about the planets
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine "Let's start our lesson with a prayer. Who can lead us in prayer?" "Good morning, class. I hope you're all ready to learn about the planets today." "Please take out your materials and get ready for the lesson." "Can our class secretary please report on the attendance?" Students participate in the prayer, greet the teacher, prepare their materials, and listen to the attendance report
Review "What is the biggest planet in our solar system?" "What is the planet we live on called?" Students answer: "Jupiter is the biggest planet" and "We live on Earth"
Motivation "Planet Scavenger Hunt" - Show students a picture of the solar system and ask them to find and identify the planets. Provide clues and riddles to make it more engaging. Students participate in the scavenger hunt and identify the planets
Lesson Proper "A planet is a big rock that goes around the sun. Can anyone tell me the names of the planets in our solar system?" Write the names of the planets on the board and have students repeat after you. Show pictures or models of the planets and ask students to identify them. Students recall the names of the planets: "Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune"
Application "Planet Sorting Game" - Divide the class into groups and give each group a set of planet cards. Ask them to sort the planets into categories (e.g. rocky planets, gas giants). Provide a rubric with criteria: accuracy (3 points), teamwork (2 points), and presentation (1 point). Students sort the planets into categories and present their work to the class
Generalization "What did you learn about the planets today?" "How can you apply what you learned about the planets in your daily life?" "Why is it important to learn about the planets?" Students share what they learned, how they can apply it, and why it's important
V. EVALUATION
Category Description
1. Multiple Choice What is the largest planet in our solar system? A) Earth, B) Saturn, C) Jupiter, D) Uranus
2. Short Answer What is the planet that we live on?
3. Identification Identify the planets in the picture provided
4. Essay Describe your favorite planet and why you like it. Provide a rubric with criteria: content (4 points), organization (3 points), and grammar (3 points).
5. Performance Task Create a model of the solar system using different materials. Provide a rubric with criteria: accuracy (4 points), creativity (3 points), and presentation (3 points).
ANSWER KEY
1. C) Jupiter

Science textbook Grade 2 Science textbook, chapter on Planets

Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response

1. C) Jupiter
2. Earth
3. The planets are arranged in the following order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune

lesson_plan:
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards: English Language Arts, Grade 9, Quarter 1
Performance Standards: Students will be able to identify and explain the characteristics of nouns.
Learning Competencies: Identify and explain the characteristics of nouns.
Cognitive/Psychomotor/Affective Objectives: Students will be able to recall and apply the characteristics of nouns through a group task.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter: Nouns, including proper nouns, common nouns, and collective nouns.
References: DepEd Order No. 10, s. 2024, MATATAG Curriculum
Materials: Whiteboard, markers, handouts with examples of nouns, and a worksheet for the group task.
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Textbook: English Language Arts, Grade 9, Quarter 1
Online Resources: Grammarly, English Central
Audio-Visual Aids: Video on nouns, animations on noun types
Manipulatives: Flashcards with examples of nouns
Games: Noun-themed board game, noun scavenger hunt
Software: Language learning software with noun exercises
Other: Worksheet with noun exercises, handouts with examples of nouns
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer, greetings, management, attendance Students will participate in the routine activities.
Review Review of previous lessons on nouns, 2-3 questions on nouns Students will answer the review questions correctly.
Motivation Activity on nouns, such as a noun-themed game or scavenger hunt Students will participate in the activity and show enthusiasm for learning about nouns.
Lesson Proper Definitions and examples of nouns, including proper nouns, common nouns, and collective nouns Students will understand the definitions and examples of nouns.
Application Group task on nouns, such as identifying and categorizing nouns Students will apply their knowledge of nouns in the group task.
Generalization Cognitive, psychomotor, and affective questions on nouns Students will answer the questions correctly and demonstrate their understanding of nouns.
V. EVALUATION
1. What is a noun? Answer: A noun is a word that refers to a person, place, thing, or idea.
2. Give an example of a proper noun. Answer: The Philippines.
3. What is a collective noun? Answer: A collective noun is a noun that refers to a group of people, animals, or things.
4. Identify the type of noun in the sentence: "The cat is sleeping on the mat." Answer: The nouns in the sentence are "cat" and "mat", which are common nouns.
5. What is the difference between a noun and a verb? Answer: A noun refers to a person, place, thing, or idea, while a verb refers to an action or a state of being.
ANSWER KEY
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task: Write a short paragraph using at least five different types of nouns.
Due Date: Next class
VII. REMARKS
Lesson Delivery: The lesson was delivered effectively, and the students were engaged throughout the activity.
Engagement: The students were actively participating in the lesson, and their enthusiasm for learning about nouns was evident.
VIII. REFLECTION
What worked: The group task on nouns was effective in engaging the students and helping them apply their knowledge of nouns.
Improvements: Provide more examples of nouns and encourage students to ask questions during the lesson.
Learner Response: The students showed enthusiasm for learning about nouns and were able to apply their knowledge in the group task.

Materials Whiteboard, Markers, Printed copies of Noun examples
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
English Module for Grade 9 DepEd-developed module for teaching English to Grade 9 students
Noun Chart Visual aid for illustrating different types of nouns
Online Dictionary Website for looking up word definitions and examples
Worksheet on Nouns Printed or digital worksheet for practicing noun identification
Video on Noun Types Online video explaining the different types of nouns
Picture Dictionary Visual aid for illustrating noun meanings through images
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer, Greetings, Classroom Management, Attendance with real dialogue Students participate in routine activities
Review Review 2-3 specific questions about previous lesson connected to Nouns Students recall previous lesson on Nouns
Motivation Noun Scavenger Hunt - Mechanics: Divide students into groups, give each group a list of nouns to find in the classroom, the group that finds the most nouns wins Students are motivated to learn about Nouns
Lesson Proper Define nouns, provide examples, answer Q&A dialogue about Nouns Students understand the concept of Nouns
Application Group Task: Read a short passage, identify and label the nouns, write a short paragraph using the nouns Students apply their understanding of Nouns
Generalization Ask Cognitive "What did you learn about Nouns?", Psychomotor "How can you apply Nouns?", Affective "Why is Nouns important?" Students generalize their understanding of Nouns
V. EVALUATION
Item Number Item Description
1 What is a noun?
2 Give an example of a common noun.
3 What is the difference between a concrete and abstract noun?
4 Identify the nouns in the following sentence: "The cat sat on the mat."
5 Write a short paragraph using at least three different types of nouns.
Item Number Correct Answer
1 A word that refers to a person, place, thing, or idea.
2 Animal.
3 A concrete noun is a noun that can be touched or seen, while an abstract noun is a noun that cannot be touched or seen.
4 cat, mat
5 (Sample paragraph: The big brown dog ran quickly around the corner of the house. The dog's owner, a young girl, laughed and chased after him. The house was old and had a big garden in the back.)
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Assignment Description
Write a short story using at least five different types of nouns. Students will write a short story using different types of nouns, such as common nouns, proper nouns, concrete nouns, and abstract nouns.
Criteria Points
Use of different types of nouns 20 points
Clarity and coherence of the story 20 points
Grammar and spelling 20 points
Overall creativity and engagement 40 points
VII. REMARKS
Aspect Remark
Lesson Execution The lesson was well-organized and engaging, with clear explanations and examples.
Learner Engagement Students were actively participating and showing interest in the lesson.
Instructional Effectiveness The lesson effectively met the learning objectives and outcomes.
Areas for Improvement Some students struggled with the concept of abstract nouns, and additional support may be needed.
VIII. REFLECTION
Aspect Reflection
What went well in this lesson The lesson was well-organized and engaging, with clear explanations and examples.
What could be improved Providing additional support for students who struggled with the concept of abstract nouns.
How learners responded to Nouns Students were actively participating and showing interest in the lesson.
Recommendations for the next lesson Building on the concept of abstract nouns, and providing more opportunities for students to practice and apply their understanding.

lesson_plan:
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards Demonstrate understanding of noun phrases, including common and proper nouns, collective nouns, and abstract nouns.
Performance Standards Identify and use nouns in sentences, including subject-verb agreement and noun modification.
Learning Competencies MAPEH-LE-01: Demonstrate understanding of language structures and vocabulary.
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to recall and identify different types of nouns.
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to use nouns correctly in sentences.
Affective Objective At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the importance of nouns in language communication.
II. SUBJECT MATTER
Subject Matter Nouns
III. MATERIALS
Materials Whiteboard, Markers, Printed copies of noun examples, Handouts with noun exercises
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Expected Student Response
Routine Prayer, Greetings, Classroom Management, Attendance Students will respond to the teacher's questions and participate in the routine activities.
Review Review of previous lesson on nouns, asking 2-3 specific questions Students will recall and identify different types of nouns.
Motivation "Noun Scavenger Hunt" - students will find and identify nouns in the classroom Students will be motivated to learn about nouns and participate in the activity.
Lesson Proper Definition and examples of nouns, Q&A dialogue Students will understand the definition and examples of nouns.
Application Group task: students will write sentences using different types of nouns Students will apply their understanding of nouns by writing sentences.
Generalization Cognitive: "What did you learn about nouns?", Psychomotor: "How can you apply nouns?", Affective: "Why is nouns important?" Students will generalize their understanding of nouns and reflect on their learning.
V. EVALUATION
Item Description Answer Key
1 What is a noun? A word that refers to a person, place, thing, or idea.
2 Give an example of a common noun. Book
3 What is a proper noun? A word that refers to a specific person, place, or thing.
4 Give an example of a collective noun. Team
5 What is an abstract noun? A word that refers to an idea or feeling.
VI. REFERENCES
Reference Description
DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020 K-12 Curriculum Guidelines
DepEd Memorandum No. 12, s. 2020 Guidelines for the Implementation of the K-12 Curriculum

lesson_plan:
Subject English
Grade Level Grade 9
Topic Nouns
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
Difficulty Basic
Special Notes None
Objectives
  • Students will be able to define and identify nouns.
  • Students will be able to classify nouns into proper and common nouns.
  • Students will be able to use nouns in a sentence.
Motivation

The teacher will show a picture of a city and ask students if they know what the different things in the picture are called.

Lesson Proper

  1. The teacher will introduce the concept of nouns and provide examples of different types of nouns.

  2. The teacher will give a quiz to check students' understanding of nouns.

  3. The teacher will provide a worksheet with sentences and ask students to identify the nouns.

  4. The teacher will provide a handout with examples of proper and common nouns and ask students to classify them.

Application

The teacher will ask students to create their own sentences using nouns.

Evaluation
Quiz
1. What is a noun? Answer: A word that refers to a person, place, or thing.
2. What is a proper noun? Answer: A noun that begins with a capital letter and refers to a specific person, place, or thing.
3. What is a common noun? Answer: A noun that refers to a general category of people, places, or things.
Worksheet
Sentence Answer
The capital of the Philippines is Manila. Manila (proper noun)
The city is crowded. city (common noun)
Assignment

Students will create their own sentences using nouns and submit them to the teacher.

Remarks

The teacher will provide feedback on students' work and encourage them to continue practicing their understanding of nouns.

Reflection

The teacher will reflect on the effectiveness of the lesson and make adjustments for future lessons.

lesson_plan:
Lesson Plan for Grade 9 English
Subject Grade Level Topic Quarter Duration
English Grade 9 Nouns 1 45 Minutes
I. Objectives
At the end of the lesson, the students will be able to:
1. Define and identify nouns in sentences.
2. Classify nouns into proper and common nouns.
3. Use nouns correctly in sentences.
II. Motivation (5 minutes)
Introduce the topic by asking students to share their favorite places or things.
Write their responses on the board and identify the nouns.
III. Lesson Proper (20 minutes)
Define and explain the concept of nouns.
Discuss the classification of nouns into proper and common nouns.
Provide examples and have students work in pairs to identify and classify nouns.
IV. Application (10 minutes)
Have students create their own sentences using nouns.
Allow students to share their sentences with the class.
V. Evaluation
Type: Quiz
Instructions: Identify the nouns in the following sentences.
Sentences:
1. The teacher is writing on the board.
2. The city of Manila is the capital of the Philippines.
3. The students are reading their books.
Answer Key:
1. teacher, board
2. city, Manila, Philippines
3. students, books
VI. Assignment
Have students create a short paragraph using at least 5 nouns.
VII. Remarks
None
VIII. Reflection
What did I learn from this lesson?
What challenges did I face and how did I overcome them?

Objectives
  • Students will be able to define and identify nouns.
  • Students will be able to classify nouns into proper and common nouns.
  • Students will be able to use nouns in a sentence.
Motivation

Nouns are words that represent people, places, and things. They are an essential part of our language. Let's learn more about nouns!
Lesson Proper
  1. Introduction (5 minutes)
  2. Direct Instruction (10 minutes)
  3. Guided Practice (15 minutes)
  4. Independent Practice (10 minutes)
  5. Conclusion (5 minutes)
Direct Instruction
  • Define nouns and provide examples.
  • Explain the difference between proper and common nouns.
  • Provide examples of nouns in a sentence.
Guided Practice
  • Have students work in pairs to identify nouns in a sentence.
  • Have students classify nouns into proper and common nouns.
Independent Practice
  • Have students write their own sentence using nouns.
  • Have students identify and classify nouns in a given text.
Application

Students will apply their knowledge of nouns in a real-life scenario.
Evaluation

Quiz: Identify and classify nouns.

Item Answer
What is a noun? A word that represents a person, place, or thing.
What is the difference between a proper noun and a common noun? A proper noun is a name of a specific person, place, or thing, while a common noun is a general term.
Write a sentence using a noun. The teacher is standing in front of the classroom.
Assignment

Write a short paragraph using at least five nouns.
Remarks

Students will be given feedback on their performance.
Reflection

What did you learn about nouns today?

  • Students will be able to classify nouns into proper and common nouns.
  • Students will be able to use nouns in a sentence.
Motivation

Nouns are words that represent people, places, and things. They are an essential part of our language. Let's learn more about nouns!
Lesson Proper
  1. Introduction (5 minutes)
  2. Direct Instruction (10 minutes)
  3. Guided Practice (15 minutes)
  4. Independent Practice (10 minutes)
  5. Conclusion (5 minutes)
Direct Instruction
  • Define nouns and provide examples.
  • Explain the difference between proper and common nouns.
  • Provide examples of nouns in a sentence.
Guided Practice
  • Have students work in pairs to identify nouns in a sentence.
  • Have students classify nouns into proper and common nouns.
Independent Practice
  • Have students write their own sentence using nouns.
  • Have students identify and classify nouns in a given text.
Application

Students will apply their knowledge of nouns in a real-life scenario.
Evaluation

Quiz: Identify and classify nouns.

Item Answer
What is a noun? A word that represents a person, place, or thing.
What is the difference between a proper noun and a common noun? A proper noun is a name of a specific person, place, or thing, while a common noun is a general term.
Write a sentence using a noun. The teacher is standing in front of the classroom.
Assignment

Write a short paragraph using at least five nouns.
Remarks

Students will be given feedback on their performance.
Reflection

What did you learn about nouns today?

Science 1 1st Quarter 45 Minutes semi MELC
I. OBJECTIVES
Category Description
Content Standards At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to:
Learning Competencies Identify the characteristics of plants using Bloom's Revised Taxonomy verb (classify) and specific outcome (types of plants).
Cognitive Objective Explain the life cycle of plants using a diagram and specific outcome (growth stages).
Psychomotor Objective Demonstrate the process of photosynthesis using a model and specific outcome (plant needs).
Affective Objective Appreciate the importance of plants in our ecosystem using a poster and specific outcome (ecological benefits).
II. CONTENT
Category Description
Subject Matter Plants
References DepEd Order No. 42, s. 2016 - Curriculum Guide for Grade 1 Science
Materials Picture cards of different types of plants, diagrams of plant life cycle, model of photosynthesis, poster about ecological benefits of plants
Values Infused Care for the environment, appreciation for nature
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description
Picture cards Visual aids for identifying different types of plants
Diagrams Visual aids for explaining plant life cycle
Model Hands-on aid for demonstrating photosynthesis
Poster Visual aid for appreciating ecological benefits of plants
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Content
Routine Prayer, Greetings, Classroom Management, Attendance - fully scripted
Review What are the different types of plants? What is the life cycle of plants?
Motivation Plant scavenger hunt - students search for different types of plants in the classroom
Lesson Proper Explanation of plant life cycle, photosynthesis, and ecological benefits
Application Students work in groups to create a diagram of plant life cycle and a poster about ecological benefits of plants
Generalization What did you learn about plants? How can you apply what you learned about plants? Why is it important to appreciate plants?
V. EVALUATION
Item Description
1 What are the different types of plants?
2 What is the life cycle of plants?
3 What is photosynthesis?
4 What are the ecological benefits of plants?
5 Can you draw a diagram of a plant life cycle?
ANSWER KEY
1 Types of plants include trees, flowers, and vegetables.
2 The life cycle of plants includes germination, growth, reproduction, and decay.
3 Photosynthesis is the process by which plants make food from sunlight, water, and air.
4 The ecological benefits of plants include providing oxygen, food, and shelter.
5 A diagram of a plant life cycle should include germination, growth, reproduction, and decay.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Create a poster about the importance of plants in our ecosystem.
Rubric
Criteria Point Value
Content 10
Design 10
Organization 10
Language 10
Score Descriptor 90-100: Excellent, 80-89: Good, 70-79: Fair, 69 and below: Needs Improvement
VII. REMARKS
The lesson was delivered smoothly and the students were engaged throughout the activity.
VIII. REFLECTION
The lesson achieved its objectives and the students demonstrated a good understanding of the topic.

CategoryDescription
Content StandardsAt the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to:
Performance StandardsAt the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to:
Learning CompetenciesAt the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to:
Cognitive ObjectiveExplain the characteristics of common nouns (e.g., person, place, thing) using examples.
Psychomotor ObjectiveDemonstrate the correct use of common nouns in sentences.
Affective ObjectiveAppreciate the importance of common nouns in effective communication.
II. CONTENT
CategoryDescription
Subject MatterNouns
ReferencesDepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020

Values InfusedImportance of effective communication

ResourceDescription
TextbookEnglish for Grade 9
Online ResourcesDepEd Online Resources
Audio-Visual AidsVideo on Nouns
TechnologyComputer with internet connection
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
StepTeacher ActivityStudent Activity
RoutinePrayer, Greetings, Classroom Management, AttendanceStudents stand up, greet each other, and take their seats.
ReviewReview previous lesson on nounsWhat are common nouns? Can you give an example?
MotivationNoun BingoStudents play noun bingo and identify common nouns.
Lesson ProperExplain characteristics of common nounsWhat are the characteristics of common nouns? Can you give an example?
ApplicationGroup activity: Identify common nouns in sentencesGroup 1: Identify common nouns in the sentence "The dog is barking." Group 2: Identify common nouns in the sentence "The teacher is writing on the board." Group 3: Identify common nouns in the sentence "The students are playing soccer." Group 4: Identify common nouns in the sentence "The city is busy." Rubric: 1 point for each correct answer.
GeneralizationCognitive question: What did you learn about nouns?Students respond: "We learned about common nouns and their characteristics." Psychomotor question: How can you apply nouns? Students respond: "We can apply nouns by using them in sentences and identifying them in texts." Affective question: Why is nouns important? Students respond: "Nouns are important because they help us communicate effectively."
V. EVALUATION
No.Description
1Identify common nouns in a sentence.
2Explain the characteristics of common nouns.
3Use common nouns in a sentence.
4Identify the type of noun (common or proper) in a sentence.
5Explain the importance of common nouns in effective communication.
ANSWER KEY
1Common nouns are words that refer to general categories of people, places, or things.
2Common nouns have no capital letters and are used to refer to general categories of people, places, or things.
3The dog is a common noun.
4The word "man" is a common noun.
5Common nouns help us communicate effectively by allowing us to refer to general categories of people, places, or things.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
TaskDescription
Write a paragraph using at least 5 common nouns.Students will write a paragraph using at least 5 common nouns and explain the characteristics of each noun.
Rubric1 point for each common noun used correctly, 1 point for explaining the characteristics of each noun.
VII. REMARKS
Teacher ObservationDescription
Students were engaged and participated actively in the lesson.Students were able to identify common nouns and explain their characteristics.
VIII. REFLECTION
Teacher ReflectionDescription
The lesson was effective in teaching students about common nouns.The students were able to apply their knowledge of common nouns in a group activity.
