Subject Grade Level Topic Quarter Duration Curriculum Difficulty Special Notes
Science Grade 8 Plants 1 45 Minutes K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Basic None
Objectives Grade Level Competencies Curriculum Framework
  • Explain the basic needs of plants.
  • Identify the different parts of a plant.
  • Describe the importance of plants in our ecosystem.
  • SC.8.L.1: Explain the basic needs of living organisms.
  • SC.8.L.2: Identify the different parts of a plant and their functions.
  • MATATAG Competency: Scientific and Technological Literacy
  • MATATAG Competency: Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving
Motivation Materials Procedure

Show a picture of a plant and ask students if they know what it needs to survive.
  • Picture of a plant
  • Whiteboard and markers
  • Plant diagram printout
  1. Ask students to share what they know about plants.
  2. Show the picture of the plant and ask students to identify the different parts.
  3. Use the whiteboard to draw a diagram of the plant and label its different parts.
  4. Distribute the plant diagram printout and have students work in pairs to match the different parts with their functions.
Application Activity Materials Procedure
Science Plant Diagram Matching
  • Plant diagram printout
  • Scissors
  • Glue
  1. Have students work in pairs to match the different parts of the plant with their functions.
  2. Have students cut out the different parts of the plant and glue them onto the corresponding functions.
Evaluation Quiz Answer Key
Science Short-Answer Test
  • What are the basic needs of plants?
  • Identify the different parts of a plant and their functions.
  • Answer 1: Water, sunlight, and air.
  • Answer 2: Root, stem, leaves, and flowers.
Assignment Task Due Date
Science Draw and label a plant diagram. Next class
Remarks Reflection
Students were able to identify the different parts of a plant and their functions.

What did I learn today?

What do I need to work on?

Science Grade 8 Plants 1 45 Minutes K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Basic None
Objectives
  • Explain the basic needs of plants.
  • Identify the different parts of a plant.
  • Describe the process of photosynthesis.
Motivation

Show a picture of a plant and ask students if they know what it needs to survive.
Lesson Proper
  1. Introduce the basic needs of plants (water, sunlight, air, and soil).
  2. Have students identify the different parts of a plant (roots, stem, leaves, and flowers).
  3. Explain the process of photosynthesis using simple diagrams and examples.
  4. Have students work in pairs to match the different parts of a plant with their functions.
Application

Have students create a diagram of a plant and label its different parts.
Evaluation

Matching Activity: Match the different parts of a plant with their functions.

Parts of a Plant Functions
Roots
Stem
Leaves
Flowers

Answer Key:

Parts of a Plant Functions
Roots Hold the plant in place and absorb water and nutrients.
Stem Support the plant and transport water and nutrients to the leaves.
Leaves Make food for the plant through photosynthesis.
Flowers Produce seeds and attract pollinators.
Assignment

Have students create a diagram of a plant and label its different parts.
Remarks

Remind students to label their diagrams clearly and accurately.
Reflection

Have students reflect on what they learned about plants and how they can apply it in their daily lives.

  1. Label the different parts of a plant.

  • Have students create a diagram of a plant and label its different parts.

School Name
Teacher Name
Subject English
Grade Level Grade 7
Date
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Lesson Plan Type D-DLP
Difficulty Intermediate
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards
Performance Standards
Learning Competencies
Cognitive Objective At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to identify the different types of characters in a story.
Psychomotor Objective At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to demonstrate an understanding of the characteristics of a main character.
Affective Objective At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to appreciate the importance of character development in a story.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter Types of Characters
References DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020. (n.d.). K-12 Curriculum Guide. Retrieved from https://www.deped.gov.ph/k-12-curriculum-guide/
Materials Whiteboard, Markers, Handouts with examples of different types of characters
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description or URL
DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020 K-12 Curriculum Guide
English textbook Grade 7 English textbook by [Author], [Edition]
Online resources Website with examples of different types of characters
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
1 Prayer: "Good morning, class. Let's start our day with a prayer. Please join me in saying the Lord's Prayer." Students repeat the Lord's Prayer
2 Greetings: "Good morning, class. How are you all doing today?" Students respond with a greeting, e.g. "Good morning, ma'am. I'm doing well, thank you."
3 Classroom Management: "Okay, class. Please take out your handouts and turn to page 3. We're going to discuss the different types of characters in a story." Students take out their handouts and turn to page 3
4 Attendance: "Okay, class. Let's take attendance. Please raise your hand if you're present." Students raise their hands if they're present
5 Review: "Okay, class. Last time we discussed the main character. Can anyone tell me what a main character is?" Student 1: "A main character is the protagonist of the story." Student 2: "Yes, ma'am. The main character is the one who drives the plot forward."
6 Motivation: "Okay, class. Let's play a game to review the different types of characters. We'll call it 'Character Charades'." Students act out different types of characters, e.g. a main character, an antagonist, a supporting character
7 Lesson Proper: "Okay, class. Now that we've reviewed the different types of characters, let's discuss the characteristics of a main character. Can anyone tell me what makes a main character different from other characters?" Student 1: "A main character has a clear goal and motivation." Student 2: "Yes, ma'am. A main character also has a clear conflict and resolution."
8 Application: "Okay, class. Now that we've discussed the characteristics of a main character, let's apply what we've learned. We'll divide into groups and create a character profile for a main character." Group 1: Creates a character profile for a main character, including their goal, motivation, conflict, and resolution. Group 2: Creates a character profile for a main character, including their goal, motivation, conflict, and resolution.
9 Generalization: "Okay, class. Now that we've applied what we've learned, let's summarize the lesson. What did you learn about main characters today?" Student 1: "I learned that a main character has a clear goal and motivation." Student 2: "Yes, ma'am. I also learned that a main character has a clear conflict and resolution."
V. EVALUATION
Item Number Item Text
1 What is the main character in a story?
2 What are the characteristics of a main character?
3 Can you give an example of a main character in a story?
4 What makes a main character different from other characters?
5 Can you create a character profile for a main character?
ANSWER KEY
Item Number Correct Answer
1 The main character is the protagonist of the story.
2 A main character has a clear goal and motivation, a clear conflict and resolution, and is the central figure in the story.
3 Example: The main character in the story "To Kill a Mockingbird" is Scout Finch.
4 A main character has a clear goal and motivation, a clear conflict and resolution, and is the central figure in the story.
5 Example: A character profile for a main character might include their name, age, occupation, goal, motivation, conflict, and resolution.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Assignment Create a character profile for a main character in a story of your choice.
Rubric Character Profile Rubric
Criteria 1. Clear goal and motivation (10 points) 2. Clear conflict and resolution (10 points) 3. Central figure in the story (10 points) 4. Well-written and organized (10 points)
VII. REMARKS
Remarks The students were able to identify the different types of characters in a story and create a character profile for a main character.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection I was able to effectively teach the students about the different types of characters in a story and help them create a character profile for a main character.

Content Standards
Performance Standards

Subject MatterTypes of Characters

TextbookGrade 7 English Language Arts textbook

HandoutsExamples of different types of characters

StepTeacher ActivityStudent Activity
1Prayer and GreetingsStudents will participate in prayer and greetings.
2Review of previous lessonStudents will review the previous lesson on character development.

4Lesson ProperStudents will learn about the different types of characters and their characteristics.
5ApplicationStudents will work in groups to identify and describe the characteristics of a well-developed character.
6GeneralizationStudents will participate in a class discussion on the importance of character development in a story.

Item NumberItem Text
1What are the different types of characters?
2Describe the characteristics of a well-developed character.
3Why is character development important in a story?
4Identify and describe the characteristics of a static character.
5Identify and describe the characteristics of a dynamic character.

1Protagonist, Antagonist, Supporting Character
2Well-developed characters have a clear motivation, goal, and conflict.
3Character development helps readers understand the characters' thoughts and feelings.
4A static character does not change or grow throughout the story.
5A dynamic character changes or grows throughout the story.

Point Value10 points

Teacher's ObservationThe students were able to identify and describe the characteristics of different types of characters.
VIII. REFLECTION
Teacher's ReflectionThe lesson was successful in teaching the students about the different types of characters and their characteristics.

lesson_plan:
Subject English
Grade Level Grade 7
Topic Types of Characters
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
Difficulty Intermediate
Special Notes None
Objectives
  • Students will be able to identify and describe the characteristics of different types of characters.
  • Students will be able to analyze and interpret the roles of characters in a story.
Motivation
  • Introduction to the topic: Ask students about their favorite characters in books or movies.
  • Discussion: Show examples of different types of characters and ask students to identify them.
Lesson Proper
  • Direct Instruction: Explain the characteristics of different types of characters (protagonist, antagonist, flat character, round character).
  • Guided Practice: Provide examples of stories with different types of characters and ask students to identify and describe them.
  • Independent Practice: Ask students to create their own stories with different types of characters.
Application
  • Ask students to apply their knowledge of character types to a real-life situation.
  • Have students create a character map to illustrate the relationships between characters in a story.
Evaluation
  • Short-answer test: Ask students to describe the characteristics of a protagonist and an antagonist.
  • Identification test: Provide examples of different types of characters and ask students to identify them.
Answer Key
  • Short-answer test:
    • Protagonist: The main character who drives the plot forward.
    • Antagonist: The character who opposes the protagonist.
  • Identification test:
    • Protagonist: The main character who drives the plot forward.
    • Antagonist: The character who opposes the protagonist.
    • Flat character: A one-dimensional character with no development.
    • Round character: A complex character with multiple traits and characteristics.
Assignment
  • Ask students to create a short story with at least two different types of characters.
  • Have students create a character map to illustrate the relationships between characters in a story.
Remarks
  • Encourage students to use their creativity when creating their own stories.
  • Remind students to use proper grammar and spelling when writing their stories.
Reflection
  • Ask students to reflect on what they learned about character types.
  • Have students write a short paragraph about how they can apply their knowledge of character types to real-life situations.

  • Ask students to create a short story with at least two different types of characters.
  • Have students create a character map to illustrate the relationships between characters in a story.

  • Encourage students to use their creativity when creating their own stories.
  • Remind students to use proper grammar and spelling when writing their stories.

  • Ask students to reflect on what they learned about character types.
  • Have students write a short paragraph about how they can apply their knowledge of character types to real-life situations.

Subject English
Grade Level Grade 7
Topic Types of Characters
Quarter 1
Duration 45 Minutes
Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
Difficulty Intermediate
Special Notes None
Objectives
  • Students will be able to identify and explain the characteristics of different types of characters.
  • Students will be able to analyze and evaluate the roles of characters in a story.
  • Students will be able to create a character profile using the characteristics of different types of characters.
Motivation
  • Introduce the topic by asking students if they have a favorite character in a book or movie.
  • Discuss the characteristics of the character and how they relate to the story.
  • Ask students to share their thoughts and ideas about characters.
Lesson Proper
  • Direct Instruction: Show examples of different types of characters (e.g. protagonist, antagonist, static character) and explain their characteristics.
  • Guided Practice: Provide students with a handout containing a short story with different types of characters. Ask students to identify and explain the characteristics of each character.
  • Independent Practice: Ask students to create a character profile using the characteristics of different types of characters.
Application
  • Ask students to create a short story featuring a character with different characteristics.
  • Have students present their short stories to the class.
Evaluation
  • Quiz: Identify the characteristics of different types of characters.
  • Short-answer test: Analyze and evaluate the roles of characters in a story.
  • Character profile: Evaluate the completeness and accuracy of the character profile.
Answer Key
  • Quiz:
    1. Protagonist: main character, often the hero
    2. Antagonist: main character, often the villain
    3. Static character: character who does not change throughout the story
  • Short-answer test:
    1. The protagonist is the main character who drives the plot forward.
    2. The antagonist is the main character who opposes the protagonist.
    3. The static character remains the same throughout the story.
  • Character profile:
    1. Name: _____________________________________
    2. Characteristics: _____________________________________
    3. Role in the story: _____________________________________
Assignment
  • Create a short story featuring a character with different characteristics.
Remarks
  • Encourage students to use their creativity when creating their short stories.
  • Provide feedback and suggestions to students on their character profiles.
Reflection
  • What did I learn about characters today?
  • How can I apply what I learned to my own writing?

I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards Types of Characters
Performance Standards Identify and describe different types of characters
Learning Competencies Recall and explain the characteristics of different types of characters
Cognitive Objective Explain the characteristics of different types of characters
Psychomotor Objective Identify and describe different types of characters through a character chart
Affective Objective Appreciate the importance of understanding different types of characters in literature
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter Types of Characters
References DepEd Grade 7 English Language Arts
Materials Whiteboard, Markers, Character Chart, Printed copies of different character types
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description or URL
Character Chart A visual aid to help students identify and describe different types of characters
Printed copies of different character types Examples of different types of characters in literature
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and ask if they have any questions or concerns. Take attendance and review the lesson plan. Students greet each other and take their seats. Students answer the teacher's questions and take attendance.
Review Review the previous lesson on types of characters. Ask students to share what they learned. Students share what they learned from the previous lesson. Students ask questions and clarify any doubts.
Motivation Show a short video clip of a character in a movie or book. Ask students to identify the type of character. Students watch the video clip and identify the type of character. Students discuss and share their answers.
Lesson Proper Explain the characteristics of different types of characters. Use the character chart to help students identify and describe different types of characters. Students listen and take notes. Students ask questions and clarify any doubts.
Application Divide students into groups and assign each group a different type of character. Ask them to create a character chart and describe the characteristics of the character. Students work in groups and create a character chart. Students describe the characteristics of the character and share with the class.
Generalization Ask students to summarize the lesson and identify the importance of understanding different types of characters in literature. Students summarize the lesson and identify the importance of understanding different types of characters in literature. Students ask questions and clarify any doubts.
V. EVALUATION
Item Number Item Text
1 What are the characteristics of a protagonist?
2 What are the characteristics of an antagonist?
3 What is the importance of understanding different types of characters in literature?
4 Identify and describe a character in a movie or book.
5 Explain the characteristics of a dynamic character.
ANSWER KEY
Item Number Correct Answer
1 A protagonist is a main character who drives the plot forward.
2 An antagonist is a character who opposes the protagonist and creates conflict.
3 Understanding different types of characters in literature helps readers analyze and interpret the story.
4 Character description: [insert character description]
5 A dynamic character is a character who changes or grows throughout the story.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Create a character chart and describe the characteristics of a character in a movie or book.
Rubric Character Chart: 20 points, Description: 30 points, Total: 50 points
VII. REMARKS
Teacher's observations and comments about the lesson.
VIII. REFLECTION
Teacher's reflective statements about the lesson.

Learning Competencies Recall and explain the characteristics of different types of characters
Cognitive Objective Explain the characteristics of different types of characters
Psychomotor Objective Identify and describe different types of characters through a character chart
Affective Objective Appreciate the importance of understanding different types of characters in literature
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter Types of Characters
References DepEd Grade 7 English Language Arts
Materials Whiteboard, Markers, Character Chart, Printed copies of different character types
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Description or URL
Character Chart A visual aid to help students identify and describe different types of characters
Printed copies of different character types Examples of different types of characters in literature
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and ask if they have any questions or concerns. Take attendance and review the lesson plan. Students greet each other and take their seats. Students answer the teacher's questions and take attendance.
Review Review the previous lesson on types of characters. Ask students to share what they learned. Students share what they learned from the previous lesson. Students ask questions and clarify any doubts.
Motivation Show a short video clip of a character in a movie or book. Ask students to identify the type of character. Students watch the video clip and identify the type of character. Students discuss and share their answers.
Lesson Proper Explain the characteristics of different types of characters. Use the character chart to help students identify and describe different types of characters. Students listen and take notes. Students ask questions and clarify any doubts.
Application Divide students into groups and assign each group a different type of character. Ask them to create a character chart and describe the characteristics of the character. Students work in groups and create a character chart. Students describe the characteristics of the character and share with the class.
Generalization Ask students to summarize the lesson and identify the importance of understanding different types of characters in literature. Students summarize the lesson and identify the importance of understanding different types of characters in literature. Students ask questions and clarify any doubts.
V. EVALUATION
Item Number Item Text
1 What are the characteristics of a protagonist?
2 What are the characteristics of an antagonist?
3 What is the importance of understanding different types of characters in literature?
4 Identify and describe a character in a movie or book.
5 Explain the characteristics of a dynamic character.
ANSWER KEY
Item Number Correct Answer
1 A protagonist is a main character who drives the plot forward.
2 An antagonist is a character who opposes the protagonist and creates conflict.
3 Understanding different types of characters in literature helps readers analyze and interpret the story.
4 Character description: [insert character description]
5 A dynamic character is a character who changes or grows throughout the story.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task Create a character chart and describe the characteristics of a character in a movie or book.
Rubric Character Chart: 20 points, Description: 30 points, Total: 50 points
VII. REMARKS
Teacher's observations and comments about the lesson.
VIII. REFLECTION
Teacher's reflective statements about the lesson.

School Name Teacher Name Subject Grade Level Date Quarter Duration Lesson Plan Type Difficulty Curriculum
Math Grade 1 1 45 Minutes D-DLP Basic K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards Performance Standards Learning Competencies Cognitive Objective Psychomotor Objective Affective Objective
MA.1.OA.1 MA.1.OA.1 MA.1.OA.1 At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to: Recall and identify numbers 1-10. At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to: Count blocks up to 10. At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to: Show appreciation for the value of addition in everyday life.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter References Materials
Addition Grade 1 Mathematics Number cards 1-10, blocks, whiteboard, markers
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Number cards 1-10, blocks, whiteboard, markers, textbook
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Prayer, Greetings, Classroom Management, Attendance Students stand up, say good morning, and greet each other. Teacher takes attendance.
Review Review previous lesson on addition using flashcards. Students take turns reviewing flashcards and saying the correct answer.
Motivation Show a picture of a shopping cart and ask students to count the items. Students count the items in the shopping cart and say the correct answer.
Lesson Proper Teach addition using number cards 1-10 and blocks. Students count the blocks and say the correct answer when the teacher asks.
Application Divide students into groups and give each group a set of number cards 1-10 and blocks. Ask them to create a simple addition problem using the materials. Students create a simple addition problem using the materials and present it to the class.
Generalization Ask students to summarize the lesson by saying one thing they learned about addition. Students say one thing they learned about addition, such as "I learned that addition is counting together."
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items
1. What is addition? _______________________________________________________
2. Count the blocks: 5 + 3 = _______________________________________________________
3. Create a simple addition problem using number cards 1-10 and blocks: _______________________________________________________
4. What is the value of addition in everyday life? _______________________________________________________
5. Count the items in the shopping cart: 8 + 2 = _______________________________________________________
ANSWER KEY
1. Addition is counting together.
2. 8
3. _______________________________________________________
4. Addition is used to count the number of items we have.
5. 10
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Assignment Task
Create a simple addition problem using number cards 1-10 and blocks. Present it to the class during the next meeting.
VII. REMARKS
The students were able to recall and identify numbers 1-10 and count blocks up to 10.
VIII. REFLECTION
I was able to effectively teach addition using number cards 1-10 and blocks. The students were engaged and participated actively in the lesson.

Math Grade 1 1 45 Minutes D-DLP Basic K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards Performance Standards Learning Competencies Cognitive Objective Psychomotor Objective Affective Objective
MA.1.OA.1 MA.1.OA.1 MA.1.OA.1 At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to: Recall and identify numbers 1-10. At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to: Count blocks up to 10. At the end of the 45 Minutes lesson, the students must be able to: Show appreciation for the value of addition in everyday life.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter References Materials
Addition Grade 1 Mathematics Number cards 1-10, blocks, whiteboard, markers
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Number cards 1-10, blocks, whiteboard, markers, textbook
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Prayer, Greetings, Classroom Management, Attendance Students stand up, say good morning, and greet each other. Teacher takes attendance.
Review Review previous lesson on addition using flashcards. Students take turns reviewing flashcards and saying the correct answer.
Motivation Show a picture of a shopping cart and ask students to count the items. Students count the items in the shopping cart and say the correct answer.
Lesson Proper Teach addition using number cards 1-10 and blocks. Students count the blocks and say the correct answer when the teacher asks.
Application Divide students into groups and give each group a set of number cards 1-10 and blocks. Ask them to create a simple addition problem using the materials. Students create a simple addition problem using the materials and present it to the class.
Generalization Ask students to summarize the lesson by saying one thing they learned about addition. Students say one thing they learned about addition, such as "I learned that addition is counting together."
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items
1. What is addition? _______________________________________________________
2. Count the blocks: 5 + 3 = _______________________________________________________
3. Create a simple addition problem using number cards 1-10 and blocks: _______________________________________________________
4. What is the value of addition in everyday life? _______________________________________________________
5. Count the items in the shopping cart: 8 + 2 = _______________________________________________________
ANSWER KEY
1. Addition is counting together.
2. 8
3. _______________________________________________________
4. Addition is used to count the number of items we have.
5. 10
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Assignment Task
Create a simple addition problem using number cards 1-10 and blocks. Present it to the class during the next meeting.
VII. REMARKS
The students were able to recall and identify numbers 1-10 and count blocks up to 10.
VIII. REFLECTION
I was able to effectively teach addition using number cards 1-10 and blocks. The students were engaged and participated actively in the lesson.

School Name Teacher Name Subject Grade Level Date Quarter Duration Lesson Plan Type Difficulty Curriculum
Math Grade 1 1 45 Minutes Detailed DLP Basic K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards 1.1 The learner demonstrates an understanding of addition as a basic mathematical operation.
Performance Standards 1.2 The learner applies addition to solve simple problems.
Learning Competencies 1.3 The learner identifies and explains the concept of addition.
Cognitive Objective 1.4 The learner recalls and applies addition facts to solve problems.
Psychomotor Objective 1.5 The learner demonstrates the ability to add numbers using manipulatives.
Affective Objective 1.6 The learner shows enthusiasm and interest in learning addition.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter Addition as a basic mathematical operation.
References DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020
Materials Number cards, addition worksheets, manipulatives
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Number cards
Addition worksheets
Manipulatives (e.g. counting blocks, buttons)
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Routine Teacher Activity Student Activity
Introduction Introduce the concept of addition and review previous lessons. Students listen and take notes.
Direct Instruction Explain the concept of addition using number cards and manipulatives. Students watch and observe.
Guided Practice Distribute addition worksheets and guide students in solving problems. Students work in pairs and share answers.
Independent Practice Provide students with manipulatives and ask them to create their own addition problems. Students create and solve their own problems.
Generalization Review and summarize the concept of addition. Students participate in a class discussion.
V. EVALUATION
1. What is addition?
2. Solve the following problem: 2 + 3 = ?
3. Create your own addition problem using manipulatives.
ANSWER KEY
1. Addition is a basic mathematical operation.
2. 5
3. (Example: 5 + 2 = ?)
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Create 5 addition problems using manipulatives and solve them.
VII. REMARKS
The lesson was successful in introducing the concept of addition to the students.
VIII. REFLECTION
I reflected on the lesson and realized that the students had difficulty understanding the concept of addition.

lesson_plan:
School Name Teacher Name Subject English Grade Level Grade 7 Date Quarter 1 Duration 45 Minutes Lesson Plan Type Detailed DLP Difficulty Intermediate Curriculum K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards Types of Characters in literature
Performance Standards Identify and describe different types of characters
Learning Competencies Recognize and analyze character traits
Cognitive Objective Students will be able to identify and describe different types of characters
Psychomotor Objective Students will be able to analyze character traits through literature
Affective Objective Students will develop appreciation for literature and its characters
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter Types of Characters in literature
References English Literature for Grade 7
Materials Textbook, whiteboard, markers
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource English Literature for Grade 7 textbook
Resource Whiteboard and markers
Resource Internet access for research
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Routine Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Introduce the topic of Types of Characters Students will take notes on the different types of characters
Reinforcement Teacher Activity Student Activity
Reinforcement Provide examples of different types of characters Students will identify and describe the character traits
Modeling Teacher Activity Student Activity
Modeling Read a passage and analyze the characters Students will analyze the characters and identify their traits
Application Teacher Activity Student Activity
Application Have students work in groups to analyze a passage Students will identify and describe the character traits
Generalization Teacher Activity Student Activity
Generalization Review the different types of characters and their traits Students will create a chart to organize the character traits
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Item What are the different types of characters in literature?
Evaluation Item Identify and describe the character traits of the protagonist in the passage.
Evaluation Item What is the difference between a static and dynamic character?
Evaluation Item How do the character traits of the characters in the passage relate to the plot?
Evaluation Item What is the significance of character development in literature?
ANSWER KEY
Answer There are several types of characters in literature, including protagonists, antagonists, static characters, and dynamic characters.
Answer The protagonist in the passage is a dynamic character because they undergo significant changes throughout the story.
Answer A static character is a character who does not change throughout the story, while a dynamic character is a character who undergoes significant changes.
Answer The character traits of the characters in the passage relate to the plot by influencing the events that occur and the outcome of the story.
Answer Character development is significant in literature because it allows readers to connect with the characters and understand their motivations and actions.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Assignment Write a short story that includes at least three different types of characters and analyze their character traits.
VII. REMARKS
Remark The students were able to identify and describe the different types of characters in literature.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection I was able to effectively teach the students about the different types of characters in literature and they were able to apply their knowledge to a short story.

School Name Teacher Name Subject Entrepreneurship Grade Level Grade 11 Date Quarter 1 Duration 60 Minutes Lesson Plan Type Detailed DLP Difficulty Advanced Curriculum MATATAG Curriculum (DepEd Order No. 10, s. 2024)
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards Entrepreneurship 11
Performance Standards Explain the concept of financial literacy and its importance in entrepreneurship.
Learning Competencies 1.1 Identify the key elements of financial literacy.
Cognitive Objective Students will be able to explain the concept of financial literacy and its importance in entrepreneurship.
Psychomotor Objective Students will be able to apply financial literacy concepts in real-life scenarios.
Affective Objective Students will develop a positive attitude towards financial literacy and entrepreneurship.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter Financial literacy, entrepreneurship, budgeting, saving, and investing.
References DepEd Order No. 10, s. 2024, Entrepreneurship Curriculum Guide.
Materials Whiteboard, markers, handouts, calculators.
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
1. Whiteboard and markers for note-taking and illustrations.
2. Handouts with financial literacy concepts and examples.
3. Calculators for budgeting and saving exercises.
4. Entrepreneurship Curriculum Guide for reference.
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
RRMLAG
Re Teacher Activity Student Activity
R Review the concept of financial literacy and its importance in entrepreneurship. Students will review their notes and handouts from previous lessons.
R Read the Entrepreneurship Curriculum Guide to understand the key elements of financial literacy. Students will read the guide and highlight the key elements of financial literacy.
M Model the application of financial literacy concepts in real-life scenarios. Students will work in groups to apply financial literacy concepts in real-life scenarios.
L Lead a class discussion on the importance of financial literacy in entrepreneurship. Students will participate in a class discussion on the importance of financial literacy in entrepreneurship.
A Assess student understanding through a quiz or test. Students will take a quiz or test to assess their understanding of financial literacy concepts.
G Guide students in creating a budget and saving plan. Students will work in groups to create a budget and saving plan.
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items 1. Students will be able to explain the concept of financial literacy and its importance in entrepreneurship.
ANSWER KEY
1. Financial literacy is the ability to understand and manage personal finances effectively.
2. Financial literacy is important in entrepreneurship because it helps entrepreneurs make informed decisions about their business.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Assignment Task:
Create a budget and saving plan for a small business.
Submit the budget and saving plan to the teacher for review.
VII. REMARKS
Students showed a good understanding of financial literacy concepts.
The class discussion was engaging and informative.
VIII. REFLECTION
As a teacher, I realized the importance of financial literacy in entrepreneurship.
I will continue to emphasize the importance of financial literacy in future lessons.

I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards: Mathematics
Performance Standards: Recognize and write numbers 1-100
Learning Competencies: Count and write numbers 1-100
Cognitive Objective: Students will be able to recognize and write numbers 1-100
Psychomotor Objective: Students will be able to write numbers 1-100 correctly
Affective Objective: Students will develop interest in mathematics
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter: Numbers 1-100
References: Mathematics textbook for Grade 1
Materials: Number cards 1-100, whiteboard, markers
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Number cards 1-100
Whiteboard and markers
Mathematics textbook for Grade 1
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
RRMLAG
Step 1: Recall Teacher Activity: Review numbers 1-10 with the students. Student Activity: Students will recall numbers 1-10 and write them on their worksheets.
Step 2: Review Teacher Activity: Review numbers 11-20 with the students. Student Activity: Students will review numbers 11-20 and write them on their worksheets.
Step 3: Model Teacher Activity: Write numbers 21-30 on the whiteboard. Student Activity: Students will observe and copy numbers 21-30 on their worksheets.
Step 4: Practice Teacher Activity: Distribute number cards 31-40 to the students. Student Activity: Students will practice writing numbers 31-40 on their worksheets.
Step 5: Application Teacher Activity: Ask students to write numbers 41-50 on their worksheets. Student Activity: Students will apply what they have learned and write numbers 41-50 on their worksheets.
Step 6: Assessment Teacher Activity: Collect worksheets and assess student understanding. Student Activity: Students will reflect on their learning and identify areas for improvement.
Step 7: Generalization Teacher Activity: Review numbers 1-100 with the students. Student Activity: Students will generalize what they have learned and apply it to real-life situations.
Step 8: Learning Activity Teacher Activity: Plan a learning activity for the next lesson. Student Activity: Students will participate in the learning activity and apply what they have learned.
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items: Students will be able to recognize and write numbers 1-100
ANSWER KEY
Answer Key: Numbers 1-100
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Assignment Task: Write numbers 51-60 on a piece of paper.
VII. REMARKS
Teacher's Remarks: The students were able to recognize and write numbers 1-100.
VIII. REFLECTION
Teacher's Reflection: The lesson was successful and the students were able to apply what they have learned.

Science Grade 3 1 45 Minutes Detailed DLP Basic K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards Science
Performance Standards Students will be able to identify and describe the basic needs of plants.
Learning Competencies Grade 3 Science
Cognitive Objective Students will be able to recall and describe the basic needs of plants.
Psychomotor Objective Students will be able to demonstrate the basic needs of plants through a diagram.
Affective Objective Students will develop an appreciation for the importance of plants in our ecosystem.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter The basic needs of plants, including sunlight, water, soil, and air.
References Science textbooks for Grade 3
Materials Whiteboard, markers, diagrams of plants, pictures of plants
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Science textbooks for Grade 3
Whiteboard, markers, diagrams of plants, pictures of plants
Internet for research
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
RRMLAG
Re Teacher Activity Student Activity
Recall Review the basic needs of plants with the students. Students will recall the basic needs of plants from their previous lessons.
Read Read the science textbook with the students and highlight the basic needs of plants. Students will read the science textbook and highlight the basic needs of plants.
Make Have the students create a diagram of a plant and label its basic needs. Students will create a diagram of a plant and label its basic needs.
Look Show the students pictures of plants and ask them to identify their basic needs. Students will look at the pictures of plants and identify their basic needs.
Act Have the students act out the basic needs of plants through a skit. Students will act out the basic needs of plants through a skit.
Discuss Discuss with the students the importance of plants in our ecosystem. Students will discuss the importance of plants in our ecosystem.
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Items Students will be evaluated based on their participation in class, their diagram of a plant, and their skit.
ANSWER KEY The basic needs of plants are sunlight, water, soil, and air.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Have the students create a poster about the basic needs of plants and display it in the classroom.
VII. REMARKS
The students were able to recall and describe the basic needs of plants.
VIII. REFLECTION
I was able to effectively teach the students about the basic needs of plants.

Science Grade 5 1 45 Minutes Detailed DLP Basic K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
Content Standards Performance Standards Learning Competencies Cognitive Objective Psychomotor Objective Affective Objective
Science Identify and describe the basic needs of plants SCIENCE 05-01-01: Identify the basic needs of plants Students will be able to identify the basic needs of plants. Students will be able to demonstrate the basic needs of plants through a diagram. Students will be able to show appreciation for the importance of plants in our daily lives.
Subject Matter References Materials
Plants DepEd materials for K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Picture of a plant, diagram of a plant, plant growth chart
Resource Source
Picture of a plant DepEd materials for K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
Diagram of a plant Internet
Plant growth chart Science textbook
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and ask if they have any questions about plants. Write their questions on the board. Students will say "Yes, I have a question about how plants grow." or "I want to know what plants need to survive."
Review Review the basic needs of plants from the previous lesson. Ask students to share what they remember. Students will say "Plants need water and sunlight to grow." or "Plants need air and water to survive."
Motivation Show students a picture of a plant and ask them to describe what they see. Write their descriptions on the board. Students will say "I see a plant with green leaves and a long stem." or "I see a plant with flowers and a big trunk."
Lesson Proper Explain to students that plants need three basic things to survive: water, sunlight, and air. Use a diagram to show students how plants absorb these needs. Students will say "I see how the roots absorb water from the soil." or "I see how the leaves absorb sunlight from the sun."
Application Ask students to create a diagram of a plant showing how it absorbs its basic needs. Have students share their diagrams with the class. Students will say "I drew a picture of a plant with roots that absorb water from the soil." or "I drew a picture of a plant with leaves that absorb sunlight from the sun."
Generalization Ask students to think about how plants are important in our daily lives. Have students share their thoughts with the class. Students will say "Plants give us oxygen to breathe." or "Plants provide us with food and shelter."
Evaluation Type Items Answer Key
Multiple Choice What are the basic needs of plants? Water, sunlight, and air
Short Answer How do plants absorb their basic needs? Through roots, leaves, and stems
Essay Why are plants important in our daily lives? Plants provide us with oxygen, food, and shelter.
Task Due Date
Create a diagram of a plant showing how it absorbs its basic needs. Next class
Observation Learners Who Need Follow-up Support What Was Accomplished
The students were able to identify the basic needs of plants. Students who struggled to create a diagram of a plant. The students were able to demonstrate their understanding of the basic needs of plants through a diagram.
Reflection Statement 1 Reflection Statement 2 Reflection Statement 3
The lesson was successful in teaching the students about the basic needs of plants. The students were able to apply their knowledge of the basic needs of plants to create a diagram. The next session will focus on teaching the students about the different types of plants and their characteristics.

Routine Welcome students and ask if they have any questions about plants. Write their questions on the board. Students will say "Yes, I have a question about how plants grow." or "I want to know what plants need to survive."
Review Review the basic needs of plants from the previous lesson. Ask students to share what they remember. Students will say "Plants need water and sunlight to grow." or "Plants need air and water to survive."
Motivation Show students a picture of a plant and ask them to describe what they see. Write their descriptions on the board. Students will say "I see a plant with green leaves and a long stem." or "I see a plant with flowers and a big trunk."
Lesson Proper Explain to students that plants need three basic things to survive: water, sunlight, and air. Use a diagram to show students how plants absorb these needs. Students will say "I see how the roots absorb water from the soil." or "I see how the leaves absorb sunlight from the sun."
Application Ask students to create a diagram of a plant showing how it absorbs its basic needs. Have students share their diagrams with the class. Students will say "I drew a picture of a plant with roots that absorb water from the soil." or "I drew a picture of a plant with leaves that absorb sunlight from the sun."
Generalization Ask students to think about how plants are important in our daily lives. Have students share their thoughts with the class. Students will say "Plants give us oxygen to breathe." or "Plants provide us with food and shelter."

School Name Teacher Name Subject Grade Date Quarter Duration Lesson Plan Type Difficulty Curriculum
Science Grade 1 1 45 Minutes S-DLP Basic K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
Content Standards Performance Standards Learning Competencies with codes Cognitive Objective Psychomotor Objective Affective Objective
Science Identify and describe the basic needs of plants. SC1P-01-01, SC1P-01-02 Students will be able to identify and describe the basic needs of plants. Students will be able to demonstrate the basic needs of plants through hands-on activities. Students will develop an appreciation for the importance of plants in our daily lives.
Subject Matter References Materials
Plants DepEd materials for K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Picture cards of plants, plant seeds, soil, water, sunlight
Resource Description
Picture cards of plants Used to identify and describe different types of plants.
Plant seeds Used to demonstrate the basic needs of plants.
Soil Used to demonstrate the basic needs of plants.
Water Used to demonstrate the basic needs of plants.
Sunlight Used to demonstrate the basic needs of plants.
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and ask if they have any questions about plants. Review the objectives of the lesson. Students will respond with questions about plants, such as "What do plants need to grow?" or "Why are plants important?"
Review Review the basic needs of plants, such as sunlight, water, and soil. Ask students to share what they already know about plants. Students will share their prior knowledge about plants, such as "Plants need sunlight to grow" or "Plants need water to drink."
Motivation Show students a picture of a plant and ask if they have ever seen a plant before. Ask students to share their favorite type of plant. Students will respond with excitement, such as "I love flowers!" or "I have a plant at home!"
Lesson Proper Distribute the materials, such as picture cards of plants, plant seeds, soil, water, and sunlight. Demonstrate how to plant a seed and explain the basic needs of plants. Students will observe and participate in the planting activity, asking questions such as "Why do plants need sunlight?" or "How do plants drink water?"
Application Ask students to create their own plant diagram, labeling the basic needs of plants. Encourage students to share their diagrams with the class. Students will create their own plant diagram, labeling the basic needs of plants, such as "Sunlight" or "Water."
Generalization Review the basic needs of plants and ask students to share what they learned. Ask students to think about how plants are important in our daily lives. Students will respond with examples of how plants are important, such as "Plants give us oxygen to breathe" or "Plants provide food for us."
Evaluation Type Items Answer Key
Multiple Choice What do plants need to grow? A) Sunlight, water, and soil
Short Answer Why are plants important in our daily lives? Plants provide oxygen, food, and shelter.
Assignment Description
Plant a seed in a pot and care for it for a week. Students will observe and record the growth of the plant, learning about the basic needs of plants.
Observation Reflection
Students were engaged and participated actively in the lesson. I was able to effectively communicate the basic needs of plants to the students, and they were able to demonstrate their understanding through their diagrams and participation in the planting activity.
Some students struggled to understand the concept of basic needs of plants. I need to provide more support and scaffolding for students who struggle with abstract concepts, such as the basic needs of plants.
Students were able to apply their knowledge of basic needs of plants to real-life situations. In the next session, I will focus on exploring the importance of plants in our daily lives and how they impact our environment.

School Name Teacher Name Subject Grade Date Quarter Duration Lesson Plan Type Difficulty Curriculum
Science Grade 1 1 45 Minutes S-DLP Basic K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020)
Content Standards Performance Standards Learning Competencies with codes Cognitive Objective Psychomotor Objective Affective Objective
Science Identify and describe basic needs of plants SC1P-1A, SC1P-1B, SC1P-1C Students will be able to identify and describe the basic needs of plants. Students will be able to demonstrate the basic needs of plants through hands-on activities. Students will develop an appreciation for the importance of plants in our daily lives.
Subject Matter References Materials
Plants DepEd materials for K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Picture cards of plants, plant seeds, soil, water, sunlight
Resource Title Resource Description
Picture cards of plants Colorful picture cards of different types of plants
Plant seeds Seeds of different types of plants
Soil Container of soil for planting seeds
Water Water for watering plants
Sunlight Window with sunlight for plants to grow
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and ask if they have any questions about plants. Introduce the topic of plants and their basic needs. What are plants? Can you show me a picture of a plant?
Review Review the basic needs of plants: sunlight, water, soil, and air. Ask students to share what they know about plants. I know plants need sunlight to grow. My mom says we need to water our plants every day.
Motivation Show students a picture of a plant and ask them to describe its basic needs. Explain that plants are important for our daily lives. Oh, I love plants! My mom has a plant in our living room. It needs sunlight and water to grow.
Lesson Proper Give each student a picture card of a plant and ask them to describe its basic needs. Demonstrate how to plant a seed in soil and water it. My plant needs sunlight and water to grow. I want to plant a seed in the soil and watch it grow.
Application Ask students to apply what they have learned by creating their own plant diagram. Use the picture cards and materials provided. I drew a picture of a plant with sunlight, water, soil, and air. My plant is happy and healthy!
Generalization Ask students to share what they have learned about plants and their basic needs. Explain that plants are important for our daily lives. I learned that plants need sunlight, water, soil, and air to grow. Plants are important for our food and oxygen.
Evaluation Type Evaluation Item Answer Key
Multiple Choice What do plants need to grow? A) Sunlight, water, soil, and air
Short Answer What is one basic need of plants? Sunlight
True or False Plants need sunlight to grow. True
Assignment Task
Draw a picture of a plant and label its basic needs. Use the picture cards and materials provided.
Remark Observation
Learner 1 Needs follow-up support on labeling the basic needs of plants.
Learner 2 Needs follow-up support on drawing a picture of a plant.
Accomplishment Students were able to identify and describe the basic needs of plants.
Reflection Statement
What worked well in this lesson? The use of picture cards and materials helped students understand the basic needs of plants.
What needs improvement in this lesson? The lesson could be improved by providing more hands-on activities for students to apply what they have learned.
What will be focused on in the next session? The next session will focus on teaching students about the different types of plants and their uses.

Routine Welcome students and introduce the topic of plants. Ask students if they have any plants at home. Students will respond with "Yes, I have a plant at home!" or "No, I don't have a plant at home."

Motivation Show students pictures of different types of plants. Ask students to identify which plants they like. Students will point to their favorite plants and say "I like that one!" or "I like that one too!"

Application Have students work in groups to create a diagram of a plant's basic needs. Ask students to label each component. Students will work together to create a diagram and label each component, such as "water," "sunlight," and "soil."
Generalization Have students present their diagrams to the class. Ask students to explain their diagrams. Students will present their diagrams and explain each component, such as "This is the water that plants need to grow."

Multiple Choice What do plants need to grow? Water, sunlight, and soil
Short Answer What is one basic need of plants? Water
True or False Plants need air to grow. True

Draw a picture of a plant's basic needs. Label each component, such as water, sunlight, and soil.

Students were engaged and participated actively in the lesson. Some students needed follow-up support in understanding the concept of basic needs of plants. The lesson was accomplished as planned.
Reflection
I was pleased with how students participated in the lesson and were able to identify and describe the basic needs of plants. However, I need to improve my explanation of the concept to ensure that all students understand it. In the next session, I will focus on providing more visual aids and hands-on activities to reinforce the concept.
I was able to assess students' understanding of the concept through the evaluation and assignment. However, I need to provide more feedback to students on their work to help them improve. In the next session, I will focus on providing constructive feedback to students on their diagrams and presentations.
I was able to incorporate technology into the lesson by showing students pictures of different types of plants. However, I need to explore more ways to incorporate technology into the lesson to make it more engaging and interactive. In the next session, I will focus on finding more educational apps and websites to use in the lesson.

lesson_plan:
Subject Science Grade Grade 1 Quarter Quarter 1 Duration 45 Minutes
Content Standards PSY 1a, PSY 1b Learning Competencies K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Cognitive Identify the basic parts of a plant. Psychomotor Plant a seedling in a pot. Affective Show appreciation for the importance of plants in our lives.
Subject Matter Plants References DepEd materials for K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Materials Picture cards of different plants, pots, seeds, gardening tools
Materials Picture cards of different plants DepEd materials for K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Pots Seeds Gardening tools
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and review the previous lesson on the life cycle of plants. Students greet the teacher and say, "Good morning, Ma'am! Yesterday, we learned about the life cycle of plants. We saw how seeds grow into plants and produce flowers and fruits."
Review Ask students to recall the basic parts of a plant. Students respond, "The basic parts of a plant are the roots, stem, and leaves. The roots help the plant drink water, the stem holds the plant up, and the leaves help the plant breathe."
Motivation Show students a picture of a beautiful garden and ask them to imagine themselves planting a seedling in a pot. Students exclaim, "Wow! I want to plant a seedling in a pot and take care of it. I want to see it grow and bloom into a beautiful flower."
Lesson Proper Explain to students the basic parts of a plant and demonstrate how to plant a seedling in a pot. Students watch and listen as the teacher explains, "The roots of the plant go into the soil, the stem holds the plant up, and the leaves help the plant breathe. Now, let's plant a seedling in a pot. First, we need to put some soil in the pot, then we need to plant the seedling, and finally, we need to water it."
Application Have students plant a seedling in a pot and take turns watering it. Students excitedly say, "I'm planting a seedling in a pot! I'm watering it! I want to see it grow and bloom into a beautiful flower."
Generalization Ask students to share what they learned about plants and how they can take care of them. Students respond, "We learned that plants need water, sunlight, and soil to grow. We can take care of plants by watering them, giving them sunlight, and making sure they have enough soil."
Evaluation Type Observation Checklist Items Answer Key
Students can identify the basic parts of a plant. Yes/No
Students can plant a seedling in a pot. Yes/No
Students can take care of a plant. Yes/No
Task Plant a seedling in a pot and take care of it for a week.
Observation The students were able to identify the basic parts of a plant and plant a seedling in a pot. However, some students needed assistance with watering the plant. Learners who need follow-up support: Students who struggled with watering the plant.
Accomplishments: Students learned about the basic parts of a plant and how to take care of it.
Reflection 1 The lesson was successful in teaching students about the basic parts of a plant and how to take care of it. However, I need to provide more assistance to students who struggle with watering the plant.
Reflection 2 I will focus on providing more hands-on activities for students to practice planting and taking care of plants.
Reflection 3 I will also provide more opportunities for students to share their experiences and observations about plants.

English Language Arts Identify and describe common nouns LE1a, LE1b, LE1c Students will be able to identify and describe common nouns in English. Students will be able to use common nouns in sentences. Students will be able to demonstrate appreciation for the importance of common nouns in English.
Subject Matter References Materials
Common Nouns DepEd materials for MELC Picture cards, flashcards, worksheets
Reference Materials Audio-Visual Materials Manipulatives Technology
English language textbooks Video clips of common nouns Picture cards, flashcards Computer with internet connection
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and review previous lesson. Students greet the teacher and review the previous lesson by saying, "Yesterday, we learned about animals."
Review Review common nouns using flashcards. Students identify common nouns on the flashcards by saying, "This is a dog."
Motivation Show a video clip of common nouns. Students watch the video clip and say, "I see a cat."
Lesson Proper Teach common nouns using picture cards. Students identify common nouns on the picture cards by saying, "This is a house."
Application Have students use common nouns in sentences. Students write sentences using common nouns, such as "The dog is happy."
Generalization Have students create a story using common nouns. Students create a story using common nouns, such as "Yesterday, I saw a cat and a dog playing together."
Evaluation Type Items Answer Key
Multiple Choice What is a common noun? 1. A proper noun 2. A common noun 3. A verb 4. An adjective 2. A common noun
Short Answer Give an example of a common noun. House
Task Due Date
Write a short paragraph using at least three common nouns. Next class
Observation Follow-up Support Accomplishment
The students were able to identify common nouns. Students who struggled with identifying common nouns will receive additional support. The students demonstrated an understanding of common nouns.

I was pleased with the students' ability to identify common nouns. However, I need to improve my teaching methods to better engage the students. In the next session, I will focus on using more interactive activities to teach common nouns.
I was able to assess the students' understanding of common nouns effectively. However, I need to provide more feedback to the students on their performance. In the next session, I will focus on providing constructive feedback to the students.
I was able to create a positive learning environment for the students. However, I need to ensure that the students are able to apply their knowledge of common nouns in real-life situations. In the next session, I will focus on providing opportunities for the students to apply their knowledge of common nouns.

Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and ask if they have any plants at home. Yes, I have a plant at home! My mom takes care of it.
Review Review the basic needs of plants. Plants need water, sunlight, and soil to grow.
Motivation Show a picture of a plant and ask students what they like about it. I like the flowers! They are so pretty.
Lesson Proper Explain the basic needs of plants and demonstrate how to plant a seedling. Wow, I can plant a seedling too! Can I help?
Application Have students plant a seedling in a pot. I'm planting my seedling! I hope it grows.
Generalization Ask students to share what they learned about plants. Plants need water, sunlight, and soil to grow. And we need to take care of them.
Evaluation Type Observation Checklist
Items Answer Key
Student plants a seedling in a pot. Yes
Student identifies the basic needs of plants. Yes
Student shows appreciation for the importance of plants in our environment. Yes
Task
Plant a seedling in a pot and take care of it for a week.
Observation Follow-up support is needed for students who had difficulty planting a seedling in a pot. The lesson was accomplished and the students learned about the basic needs of plants.
Reflection 1
The students were engaged and motivated throughout the lesson.
Reflection 2
The lesson needs improvement in terms of providing more hands-on activities for the students.
Reflection 3
The next session will focus on teaching the students how to care for their planted seedlings.

School Name Teacher Name Subject Grade Level Date Quarter Duration
Bagong Silangan Elementary School Ms. Maria Lourdes B. Santos Science Grade 1 24 May 2026 1st Quarter 45 minutes
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards Performance Standards Learning Competencies with codes Cognitive Objective Psychomotor Objective Affective Objective
1.1.1.1 1.1.1.2 1.1.1.3 - Identify and describe the basic needs of plants Students can identify and describe the basic needs of plants. Students can demonstrate the basic needs of plants through drawings and writings. Students can show appreciation and care for plants.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter References Materials
Plants DepEd materials for K-12 MELCs (DepEd Order No. 12, s. 2020) Picture cards of plants, whiteboard, markers, worksheets
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Resource Type
Picture cards of plants Visual aid
Whiteboard and markers Technology
Worksheets Printed materials
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and ask if they have any questions about plants. Students respond with their questions.
Review Review the basic needs of plants using picture cards. Students identify and describe the basic needs of plants.
Motivation Show a video about the importance of plants. Students watch and listen to the video.
Lesson Proper Teach the basic needs of plants using the whiteboard and markers. Students take notes and ask questions.
Application Distribute worksheets and have students draw and write about the basic needs of plants. Students complete the worksheets.
Generalization Have students share their worksheets with the class. Students listen and appreciate each other's work.
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Type Items Answer Key
Multiple Choice What is the basic need of plants for growth?
A) Water
B) Sunlight
C) Soil		 C) Soil
Short Answer What are the basic needs of plants? Water, sunlight, and soil
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Have students draw and write about a plant that they like and its basic needs.
VII. REMARKS
Learner Follow-up Support Accomplishment
John Needs extra support in identifying the basic needs of plants. Completed the worksheets with minimal errors.
Jane Needs to improve her drawing skills. Completed the worksheets with excellent drawings.
VIII. REFLECTION
Reflection
I was able to effectively teach the basic needs of plants to my students.
I need to improve my use of visual aids to engage my students better.
I will focus on assessing my students' understanding of the basic needs of plants in the next session.

I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards:
Performance Standards:
Learning Competencies: LC 1.1.1 LC 1.1.2
Cognitive Objective: Students will be able to identify and name common nouns.
Psychomotor Objective: Students will be able to write common nouns correctly.
Affective Objective: Students will develop an appreciation for the importance of common nouns in language.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter: Common Nouns
References: DepEd materials for Mother Tongue-Based Multilingual Education (MTB-MLE)
Materials: Picture cards of common objects, whiteboard, markers, worksheets
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Picture cards of common objects
Whiteboard and markers
Worksheets with common nouns
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Welcome students and review the previous lesson on common nouns. Students will greet the teacher and review the previous lesson.
Review Show picture cards of common objects and ask students to identify the nouns. Students will identify the nouns and give examples.
Motivation Explain the importance of common nouns in language and show examples. Students will listen and ask questions.
Lesson Proper Write common nouns on the board and ask students to write them on their worksheets. Students will write the common nouns and ask for help if needed.
Application Give students a worksheet with common nouns and ask them to identify and write the nouns. Students will complete the worksheet and ask for help if needed.
Generalization Review the common nouns and ask students to give examples of how they are used in everyday life. Students will give examples and ask questions.
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Type: Multiple Choice
Items: 1. What is a common noun? 2. Give an example of a common noun. 3. What is the importance of common nouns in language?
Answer Key: 1. A common noun is a word that refers to a general category of things. 2. Example: dog 3. Common nouns are important in language because they help us communicate and identify objects and concepts.
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task: Write a short paragraph using at least 5 common nouns.
VII. REMARKS
Learners who need follow-up support: Students who struggled with identifying and writing common nouns.
Accomplishments: Students were able to identify and write common nouns correctly.
VIII. REFLECTION
What worked well in this lesson: The use of picture cards and worksheets helped students to engage and learn the common nouns.
What needs improvement: The lesson could be improved by providing more examples and practice exercises for students to reinforce their understanding of common nouns.
What to focus on in the next session: In the next session, I will focus on teaching students how to use common nouns in sentences and provide more practice exercises to reinforce their understanding.

Content Standards Performance Standards Learning Competencies Cognitive Objective Psychomotor Objective Affective Objective

Reflection
I was able to deliver the lesson effectively and the students were able to learn about the basic needs of plants.

lesson_plan:
School Name Teacher Name Subject Grade Level Date Quarter Duration
Bagong Silang Elementary School Ms. Maria Lourdes B. Santos English Grade 2 2024-05-24 1st Quarter 45 minutes
I. OBJECTIVES
Content Standards:
Performance Standards:
Learning Competencies: LC 1.1.1 LC 1.1.2
Cognitive Objective: Students can identify and name common nouns.
Psychomotor Objective: Students can write common nouns on a piece of paper.
Affective Objective: Students will show interest in learning common nouns.
II. CONTENT
Subject Matter: Nouns
References: DepEd materials for MATATAG Curriculum (DepEd Order No. 10, s. 2024)
Materials: Picture cards of common objects, whiteboard, markers, worksheets
III. LEARNING RESOURCES
Picture cards of common objects
Whiteboard and markers
Worksheets with common noun examples
IV. LEARNING PROCEDURE
Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
Routine Good morning, class! Today, we will learn about common nouns. Students greet the teacher and take their seats.
Review What did we learn about nouns last week? Students respond with answers.
Motivation Let's look at these picture cards. Can you tell me what these are? Students point to the picture cards and say the names of the objects.
Lesson Proper These are common nouns. Can you write the names of these objects on the board? Students write the names of the objects on the board.
Application Now, let's practice writing common nouns on a piece of paper. Students write common nouns on a piece of paper.
Generalization Can you think of more common nouns? Students respond with answers.
V. EVALUATION
Evaluation Type: Multiple Choice
Items: 1. What is a common noun? 2. What is an example of a common noun?
Answer Key: 1. A common noun is a word that refers to a general category of things. 2. An example of a common noun is "dog".
VI. ASSIGNMENT
Task: Write five common nouns on a piece of paper.
VII. REMARKS
Ms. Santos observed that most students were able to identify and write common nouns.
However, some students struggled to think of more common nouns.
Ms. Santos will provide additional support to these students in the next lesson.
VIII. REFLECTION
Ms. Santos is satisfied with the lesson delivery and the students' understanding of common nouns.
However, she realizes that she needs to provide more opportunities for students to practice writing common nouns.
In the next lesson, Ms. Santos will focus on teaching students how to use common nouns in sentences.

Step Teacher Activity Student Activity
